overview.overview:
OpenCode Multiuser lets many people use OpenCode through one browser portal. A FastAPI control plane authenticates users (local accounts or generic OIDC), then starts a disposable, locked-down rootless Podman container running `opencode serve` for each project a user opens. Project files and OpenCode state live in per-user directories on the host, so the container can be destroyed and recreated without losing work. Capacity is a fixed pool of numbered slots (`MAX_SLOTS`), and containers are created on demand and removed on stop, logout or idle timeout.

The same FastAPI app is also the gateway. Traefik forwards the single public hostname to it. Requests that are not portal routes fall through to a catch-all proxy in `app/gateway.py`, which finds the user's running workspace, swaps the portal session for that container's private Basic Auth credential, and forwards HTTP and WebSocket traffic to a loopback-only port derived from the slot. `app/runtime.py` is the only code that talks to Podman, `app/models.py` and `app/migrations.py` define the PostgreSQL state, and a background reaper reconciles database leases with the containers that actually exist.

key_concepts.explanation: A `Slot` row is one unit of capacity and a `Workspace` row holds a slot while it is starting, running or stopping. A partial unique index allows only one active workspace per user and project.

Each workspace container is created fresh and removed on stop, while its workspace and OpenCode data directories are kept under the data root. The per-workspace secret, activity timestamp and stop reason are small files in that same directory.

The browser never talks to a workspace container directly. The gateway checks that the selected workspace is running and owned by the user, strips portal credentials, injects the container's Basic Auth, and adds the Portal widget to HTML pages.

The database can drift from what Podman is really running. At startup and on every reaper tick, stale leases are recycled and workspaces idle past the timeout are stopped, with the stop reason recorded so the gateway can explain it to the user.
Administrator-chosen enabled and disabled OpenCode provider lists are written to a managed config file and mounted read-only into every workspace, so users cannot override them.
`app/version.py` holds the only copy of the version number. The UI, API metadata, installer and release packaging all read it, and `scripts/version.py` edits it.

reading_order.why: Every setting the control plane understands, so the rest of the code's behaviour is easier to follow.
The users, slots and workspaces tables, including the invariants their indexes enforce.
How a workspace container is actually started, secured, health-checked and stored on disk.
The reverse proxy that turns a portal session into authenticated access to one workspace.
The routes, lifespan startup, slot release logic and idle reaper that tie everything together.
How the services, Traefik and the control-plane environment are put in place on a host.

app/__init__.py.summary: Package marker for `app` that re-exports `__version__` from `app.version`, so the version can be read as `app.__version__`. `app/version.py` remains the single place where the number is defined.

notes.text: Relative import of the version string from `app/version.py`; importing the `app` package therefore also imports that module.
`__all__` limits `from app import *` to `__version__` and marks the re-export as intentional.

app/config.py.summary: Defines the `Settings` class, a pydantic-settings model holding all configuration for the control plane: domain and ports, database, JWT and cookies, authentication (local and OIDC), Podman workspace limits, Traefik and OpenCode provider policy. A module-level `settings` instance is created at import time, so other modules just import it.

notes.text: `extra="ignore"` lets the shared `.env` hold keys this model does not define without causing a validation error.
The comment explains the default: local auth stays on so a fresh install works before OIDC is set up.

Comma-separated provider ID lists, parsed by `enabled_provider_ids` and `disabled_provider_ids`. The comment says they are applied as OpenCode managed settings to every workspace, taking precedence over project config.
`%h` is replaced by the home directory before `expanduser()`, then `resolve()` makes the path absolute.
A staticmethod so it can be used without an instance. It keeps the first occurrence of each ID, so the result is de-duplicated and keeps its order.
Both issuer and client ID must be non-blank after `strip()`, so whitespace-only values count as unset.
An explicit discovery URL wins; otherwise the standard OIDC well-known path is derived from the issuer, with a trailing slash trimmed to avoid `//`.
An explicit redirect URI wins; otherwise it is derived from `control_plane_url`, so a deployment behind a different public URL should set `oidc_redirect_uri`.
Two fail-fast checks: no usable login method, and OIDC enabled but missing its issuer or client ID.
The shared `settings` singleton is built on import, so environment and `.env` are read once when the module is first imported.

app/db.py.summary: Sets up the SQLAlchemy database layer: the declarative `Base` for models, the engine built from `settings.database_url`, the `SessionLocal` factory and the `get_db` session dependency.

notes.text: `pool_pre_ping` tests a pooled connection before it is used, so connections dropped by the server are replaced. For SQLite URLs `check_same_thread=False` is added so a connection can be used from threads other than the one that created it.
The engine is created at import time from `settings.database_url`.
`autoflush=False` stops queries from flushing pending changes on their own, and `expire_on_commit=False` keeps loaded objects usable after `commit()` without a reload.

app/gateway.py.summary: The reverse proxy between the portal's public port and the per-workspace OpenCode containers. It picks the running workspace a request belongs to, swaps the user's portal session for the workspace's Basic Auth credentials, forwards HTTP (streaming) and WebSocket traffic to the container's loopback port, and injects the portal widget into HTML pages. It also records activity on every proxied exchange, which feeds idle reclamation elsewhere.

notes.text: Hop-by-hop headers (RFC 7230) describe a single connection and must not be forwarded by a proxy.
The portal's own session and workspace-selector cookies are blocked from reaching OpenCode.

`host`, `authorization` and `content-length` are recomputed for the upstream request. `x-opencode-workspace` is dropped because the gateway authorizes workspace selection itself and must not forward a client-controlled routing header.
The client's authorization is replaced with the workspace credentials. `accept-encoding: identity` keeps responses uncompressed so HTML can be edited.
The workspace query is scoped to the current user and to `RUNNING` status. This is the authorization boundary for workspace selection.
An explicit selector may be a workspace id or a container name. A miss is reported as 404.
With no selector, a unique running workspace is chosen implicitly. Zero or several are reported as 409 with a hint on how to choose.
The header wins over the cookie, so a script can override the browser's remembered workspace.

`follow_redirects=False` lets the browser handle redirects. `timeout=None` allows long-lived streams such as server-sent events. `trust_env=False` avoids picking up proxy settings from the environment.
`stream=True` returns as soon as the headers arrive, so the body can be streamed or read depending on the content type.
The client is closed before the error is raised, since no response object will take ownership of it. The result is a 502.
Widget injection applies only to successful HTML responses. Errors, redirects and non-HTML assets are streamed through untouched.
The body is decoded using the response's encoding, modified and re-encoded. Upstream and client are closed in `finally`, and the rewritten bytes are returned as a plain `Response`.
The streaming path leaves the upstream open and closes it from a `BackgroundTask` after the response has been sent.

Headers are rebuilt from `upstream.headers.raw` so repeated headers such as `Set-Cookie` are preserved. `content-length` is dropped because the body is re-framed or rewritten, and `content-encoding` is dropped for HTML because the body has been decoded.
An absolute `Location` pointing at the loopback backend is rewritten to the public `control_plane_url`, so redirects do not leak the internal address.
WebSocket authentication accepts the session cookie, or an `Authorization: Bearer` header as fallback. A missing or invalid user closes with 4401 before anything else.

When workspace selection fails, the gateway checks whether the user's selected workspace was stopped for inactivity. If so it closes with 4409 and a readable reason so the client can send the user to the dashboard. Otherwise the original error is re-raised.
Connects upstream with the Basic credentials. `max_size=None` removes the message size limit, and `proxy=None` stops the library from using environment proxies.
The client WebSocket is accepted only after the backend connection is established, so failed connections never appear open to the browser.
The two relays run as concurrent tasks and the proxy waits for the first to finish. The remaining task is cancelled and awaited with `return_exceptions=True` so cancellation does not raise.
An error from the completed task, if any, is re-raised so the outer handler closes the socket with 1011.
Any failure closes the client socket with 1011 (internal error). Errors during that close are ignored because the socket may already be gone.

import asyncio
import base64
from typing import Iterable

import httpx
import websockets
from fastapi import HTTPException, Request, WebSocket, status
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from starlette.background import BackgroundTask
from starlette.responses import Response, StreamingResponse

from .config import settings
from .models import User, Workspace, WorkspaceStatus
from .portal import inject_portal_widget
from .runtime import read_workspace_secret, read_workspace_stop_reason, touch_workspace_activity, workspace_host_port
from .security import load_user_from_token

_HOP_BY_HOP = {
    "connection",
    "keep-alive",
    "proxy-authenticate",
    "proxy-authorization",
    "te",
    "trailer",
    "transfer-encoding",
    "upgrade",
}


def _basic_auth(password: str) -> str:
    raw = f"opencode:{password}".encode("utf-8")
    return "Basic " + base64.b64encode(raw).decode("ascii")


def _clean_cookie_header(cookie_header: str | None) -> str | None:
    if not cookie_header:
        return None
    blocked = {settings.session_cookie_name, settings.workspace_cookie_name}
    kept: list[str] = []
    for part in cookie_header.split(";"):
        item = part.strip()
        if not item or "=" not in item:
            continue
        name = item.split("=", 1)[0].strip()
        if name not in blocked:
            kept.append(item)
    return "; ".join(kept) if kept else None


def _forward_headers(headers: Iterable[tuple[str, str]], password: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    result: dict[str, str] = {}
    cookie_header: str | None = None
    for key, value in headers:
        lower = key.lower()
        if lower in _HOP_BY_HOP or lower in {"host", "authorization", "content-length"}:
            continue
        if lower == "x-opencode-workspace":
            # Selection is handled and authorized by the gateway; never forward
            # a client-controlled routing header to OpenCode.
            continue
        if lower == "cookie":
            cookie_header = value
            continue
        result[key] = value
    cleaned_cookie = _clean_cookie_header(cookie_header)
    if cleaned_cookie:
        result["cookie"] = cleaned_cookie
    result["authorization"] = _basic_auth(password)
    result["accept-encoding"] = "identity"
    return result


def _find_selected_workspace(
    *,
    user: User,
    db: Session,
    selector: str | None,
) -> Workspace:
    stmt = select(Workspace).where(
        Workspace.user_id == user.id,
        Workspace.status == WorkspaceStatus.RUNNING,
    )
    if selector:
        stmt = stmt.where(
            (Workspace.id == selector) | (Workspace.container_name == selector)
        )
        ws = db.scalar(stmt)
        if not ws:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Selected running workspace not found")
        return ws

    rows = db.scalars(stmt.order_by(Workspace.created_at.desc())).all()
    if not rows:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail="No running workspace. Start one from /dashboard.")
    if len(rows) > 1:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=409,
            detail="Multiple running workspaces. Open one from /dashboard or send X-OpenCode-Workspace.",
        )
    return rows[0]


def selected_workspace_for_request(request: Request, user: User, db: Session) -> Workspace:
    selector = request.headers.get("x-opencode-workspace") or request.cookies.get(settings.workspace_cookie_name)
    return _find_selected_workspace(user=user, db=db, selector=selector)


def selected_workspace_for_websocket(websocket: WebSocket, user: User, db: Session) -> Workspace:
    selector = websocket.headers.get("x-opencode-workspace") or websocket.cookies.get(settings.workspace_cookie_name)
    return _find_selected_workspace(user=user, db=db, selector=selector)


def _backend_http_url(ws: Workspace, request: Request) -> str:
    if ws.slot_id is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail="Workspace has no assigned slot")
    port = workspace_host_port(ws.slot_id)
    path = request.url.path
    query = request.url.query
    return f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}{path}" + (f"?{query}" if query else "")


def _backend_ws_url(ws: Workspace, websocket: WebSocket) -> str:
    if ws.slot_id is None:
        raise RuntimeError("Workspace has no assigned slot")
    port = workspace_host_port(ws.slot_id)
    path = websocket.url.path
    query = websocket.url.query
    return f"ws://127.0.0.1:{port}{path}" + (f"?{query}" if query else "")


async def proxy_http(request: Request, user: User, db: Session):
    ws = selected_workspace_for_request(request, user, db)
    touch_workspace_activity(user.id, ws.project_slug)
    password = read_workspace_secret(user.id, ws.project_slug)
    target = _backend_http_url(ws, request)
    headers = _forward_headers(request.headers.items(), password)
    body = await request.body()

    client = httpx.AsyncClient(follow_redirects=False, timeout=None, trust_env=False)
    try:
        upstream = await client.send(
            client.build_request(request.method, target, headers=headers, content=body),
            stream=True,
        )
    except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
        await client.aclose()
        detail = str(exc).strip() or "connection failed"
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=502,
            detail=f"OpenCode backend unavailable: {type(exc).__name__}: {detail}",
        ) from exc

    content_type = upstream.headers.get("content-type", "").lower()
    inject_widget = upstream.status_code == 200 and "text/html" in content_type

    if inject_widget:
        try:
            payload = await upstream.aread()
            charset = upstream.encoding or "utf-8"
            html = payload.decode(charset, errors="replace")
            body_bytes = inject_portal_widget(html, ws.project_slug).encode(charset, errors="replace")
        finally:
            await upstream.aclose()
            await client.aclose()
        response = Response(content=body_bytes, status_code=upstream.status_code)
    else:
        async def stream_upstream():
            async for chunk in upstream.aiter_raw():
                touch_workspace_activity(user.id, ws.project_slug)
                yield chunk

        async def close_upstream() -> None:
            await upstream.aclose()
            await client.aclose()

        response = StreamingResponse(
            stream_upstream(),
            status_code=upstream.status_code,
            background=BackgroundTask(close_upstream),
        )

    # Preserve duplicate response headers such as Set-Cookie. Rewrite an
    # absolute loopback redirect, if OpenCode emits one, back to the public URL.
    raw_headers: list[tuple[bytes, bytes]] = []
    backend_origin = f"http://127.0.0.1:{workspace_host_port(ws.slot_id)}"
    for key, value in upstream.headers.raw:
        lower = key.decode("latin-1").lower()
        if lower in _HOP_BY_HOP or lower == "content-length":
            continue
        # HTML bodies are decoded and rewritten by the gateway, so an upstream
        # content-encoding can no longer be forwarded verbatim. Preserve CSP:
        # the widget remains functional without JavaScript because its core
        # controls are ordinary links/forms.
        if inject_widget and lower == "content-encoding":
            continue
        if lower == "location":
            text = value.decode("latin-1")
            if text.startswith(backend_origin):
                value = (settings.control_plane_url.rstrip("/") + text[len(backend_origin):]).encode("latin-1")
        raw_headers.append((key, value))
    response.raw_headers = raw_headers
    return response


async def proxy_websocket(websocket: WebSocket, db: Session) -> None:
    token = websocket.cookies.get(settings.session_cookie_name)
    auth_header = websocket.headers.get("authorization")
    if not token and auth_header and auth_header.lower().startswith("bearer "):
        token = auth_header.split(" ", 1)[1]
    user = load_user_from_token(token, db)
    if not user:
        await websocket.close(code=4401)
        return

    try:
        try:
            ws = selected_workspace_for_websocket(websocket, user, db)
        except HTTPException:
            selector = websocket.headers.get("x-opencode-workspace") or websocket.cookies.get(settings.workspace_cookie_name)
            stopped = None
            if selector:
                stopped = db.scalar(
                    select(Workspace).where(
                        Workspace.id == selector,
                        Workspace.user_id == user.id,
                        Workspace.status == WorkspaceStatus.STOPPED,
                    )
                )
            if stopped and read_workspace_stop_reason(user.id, stopped.project_slug) == "idle":
                await websocket.close(
                    code=4409,
                    reason="Workspace stopped due to inactivity; return to /dashboard",
                )
                return
            raise
        touch_workspace_activity(user.id, ws.project_slug)
        password = read_workspace_secret(user.id, ws.project_slug)
        target = _backend_ws_url(ws, websocket)
        upstream_headers = {"Authorization": _basic_auth(password)}

        async with websockets.connect(
            target,
            additional_headers=upstream_headers,
            open_timeout=15,
            max_size=None,
            proxy=None,
        ) as upstream:
            await websocket.accept()

            async def client_to_upstream() -> None:
                while True:
                    message = await websocket.receive()
                    kind = message.get("type")
                    if kind == "websocket.disconnect":
                        break
                    if message.get("text") is not None:
                        touch_workspace_activity(user.id, ws.project_slug)
                        await upstream.send(message["text"])
                    elif message.get("bytes") is not None:
                        touch_workspace_activity(user.id, ws.project_slug)
                        await upstream.send(message["bytes"])

            async def upstream_to_client() -> None:
                async for message in upstream:
                    touch_workspace_activity(user.id, ws.project_slug)
                    if isinstance(message, bytes):
                        await websocket.send_bytes(message)
                    else:
                        await websocket.send_text(message)

            done, pending = await asyncio.wait(
                {
                    asyncio.create_task(client_to_upstream()),
                    asyncio.create_task(upstream_to_client()),
                },
                return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED,
            )
            for task in pending:
                task.cancel()
            await asyncio.gather(*pending, return_exceptions=True)
            for task in done:
                exc = task.exception()
                if exc:
                    raise exc
    except Exception:
        try:
            await websocket.close(code=1011)
        except Exception:
            pass

app/main.py.summary: `app/main.py` is the FastAPI application that acts as the control plane and gateway for OpenCode Multiuser. This part holds the workspace lease and slot bookkeeping helpers, the admin-safety helpers, the idle reaper, the startup `lifespan` (migrations, slot seeding, reconciliation), the app and session middleware setup, and the auth and login/registration routes. The rest of the file (parts 2 and 3) covers the dashboard, admin and workspace APIs, the portal widget endpoints, and the HTTP/WebSocket gateway proxy.

notes.text: A workspace is offered to the user only when it is `RUNNING` and its secret file exists. The secret file is presumably what the gateway uses to authenticate to the container, so the URL is withheld until it exists.
Collects the existing slot ids into a set so only missing ids are inserted. This makes the seeding safe to repeat on every startup.
Commits `STOPPING` before the slow container stop, so other requests and a later reconciliation can see that a release was in progress.
The values are saved in locals before the stop because the fields are cleared afterwards.
Frees the slot in the pool and unlinks it from the workspace. The `if slot_id` and `if slot` guards tolerate workspaces with no slot or a slot row that has gone missing.
Final state: stopped with timestamp, container and slot references cleared, and the stop reason written to disk. It is committed in a single transaction.
Short-circuiting `and` chain: the database and filesystem checks come first, and the container queries `container_running` and `container_has_workspace_port` come last.
Selects the in-flight states `STARTING`, `RUNNING` and `STOPPING`, because every one of them holds, or may hold, a slot and a container.
Healthy workspaces are skipped; everything else falls through to recycling.
Rows are ordered newest first within each user and project, so the first one seen is the one kept. All later rows for the same key are duplicates.
The lock is taken only on PostgreSQL, since the SQL is dialect specific. `SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE` conflicts with itself, so two admin mutations cannot run at once.
Counts rows where `role` is admin and `is_active` is true. `is_(True)` produces an explicit `IS true` comparison, and `or 0` handles a `None` result.
A user can be deleted only if the account is local, is not the requesting admin, and has never had a workspace.
Blocks the change only when the target is currently an enabled admin and is the only one left.
A timeout of zero or less turns the reaper off, which matches the check in `lifespan` before starting the task.
Falls back to `created_at` when there is no activity record. A naive datetime is assumed to be UTC so it can be compared with the timezone-aware cutoff.
The interval is clamped to at least 5 seconds so a bad setting cannot cause a busy loop.
The blocking reconcile and reap functions run in a thread pool to keep the event loop free.
`CancelledError` is re-raised so shutdown can stop the task. Any other error is logged and the loop keeps running.
The comment explains that the old uniqueness constraint must be dropped before table creation and reconciliation, using `IF EXISTS` so fresh installs work.

Startup order: validate settings, fix the schema, create tables and slots, create directories, remove legacy routes, clean up stale and duplicate workspaces, and only then create the partial index that depends on the data being deduplicated.
Since all workspaces are now routed through the gateway, Traefik files left by the earlier per-workspace routing are removed.
The background reaper starts only when idle reclamation is enabled.
On shutdown the reaper task is cancelled and awaited, and the exceptions are swallowed so shutdown is clean.
The API docs and OpenAPI schema are moved under `/_control/`, and ReDoc is disabled.

`SessionMiddleware` is used for the OIDC state (cookie name and TTL come from the OIDC settings), signed with `settings.jwt_secret`. `https_only` follows `settings.cookie_secure`. This cookie is separate from the login session cookie set by `_set_session_cookie`.
The unique constraint on the username is the source of truth for duplicates. A violation is rolled back and reported as 409.
The same 401 response is used when the user is missing and when the password is wrong.
A token response without `userinfo` is treated as an error, and the user is then provisioned or looked up from the claims.
Both expected rejections (`HTTPException`) and unexpected errors send the browser back to the login page with `error=oidc`. Only the unexpected ones are logged with a stack trace.
A 303 redirect sets the session cookie, so the browser follows it with GET to `/dashboard`.
Clears the OIDC state stored by `SessionMiddleware`.
Stopping the user's workspaces on logout depends on `settings.stop_workspaces_on_logout`.
Both the session cookie and the workspace cookie are removed, using `path="/"` to match how they were set.
The users table is checked for any row to tell whether the visitor would be the first account.
The query string selects a notice. `escape` is applied to the project name because it comes from the URL and is placed into HTML. The idle message reports the configured timeout.
Capacity shown on the dashboard is computed live from the `Slot` table.
After an idle stop the workspace cookie is dropped, so the browser no longer points at the stopped workspace.
`check_latest=False` avoids a remote call on page load. The latest version is fetched on demand by `admin_opencode_latest`.
Any failure while talking to the registry is reported as 502 Bad Gateway, with the error type and message included.
Error mapping for the update starter: invalid input gives 422, and a state conflict gives 409.
The summary is computed in Python from the loaded users and payloads, without further queries.
Lock first, then load and check. Self-demotion is blocked explicitly, and `_protect_last_admin` blocks removing the last admin.
Disabling an active user also stops the user's workspaces, so a disabled account does not keep running containers.
Password reset only applies to local accounts, because OIDC accounts have no local password.

Delete safeguards: not yourself, only local accounts, not the last enabled admin, and not anyone with workspace history. This is the same condition as `can_delete` in the payload, plus the last-admin check.
`setdefault` on newest-first rows keeps the newest workspace per project and ignores older rows.

An active workspace is reused only when it is `RUNNING`, has its secret file and has a running container. Anything else, such as a legacy v5 runtime or a stuck `STARTING` row, is recycled and started afresh.
Picks the lowest-numbered free slot. On databases other than SQLite it uses `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, so concurrent starts do not choose the same slot. No free slot gives 503.
An existing row is reused with a reset state and fresh `created_at`, which matters for the dedupe and idle logic. Otherwise a new row is added and `flush` assigns its id before the slot is linked.
The slot is marked taken and the workspace committed in `STARTING` state before the slow container start, so the reservation is visible to others.
On success the workspace becomes `RUNNING`. On failure the container is stopped, the slot is freed, and the workspace is marked `ERROR` and a 500 is raised.
Stopping an already stopped workspace is idempotent.
A live workspace is stopped first. If the data directory cannot be removed, the request fails with 500 before the row is deleted.
The stop reason is read only for stopped workspaces; it is what tells the widget that the stop came from idleness or an admin.
The workspace cookie is the only selector. The user filter in the query stops one user from stopping another's workspace.
Only a `RUNNING` workspace owned by the caller can be opened. A missing secret file means a legacy runtime that the gateway cannot authenticate to, so it must be recycled first.
Refreshes the activity timestamp so the reaper does not reclaim the workspace, then selects it with the workspace cookie and redirects to `/`.
Bearer header first, then the session cookie.
Only `GET` navigations count; `Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate` is checked first, then the `Accept` header.
The header lets API clients name a workspace; browsers rely on the cookie.
The comment says that `container_name` is cleared when a runtime stops, so the id is the selector that still works afterwards.
A workspace counts as idle-reclaimed only when the persisted stop reason is exactly `idle`.
Browsers get a friendly redirect to the dashboard. The cookie is cleared so the stopped workspace is not selected again.
API callers get a machine-readable 409 with a stable `code` instead of a redirect.
When no workspace can be selected, an idle timeout is distinguished from the general no-workspace case. Otherwise the user goes to the dashboard with the stale cookie cleared.
Request-time recovery. A selected workspace whose runtime is not usable is released, so the slot is freed, and the user is told through `reason=backend`.
The comment says that the catch-all route must be registered last, so that all control-plane routes defined above it stay local and everything else is forwarded to the OpenCode runtime.
The runtime health check happens on every proxied request. If the container is gone, the stale lease is released immediately so the slot returns to the pool.
Browsers are redirected with a readable notice on the dashboard, and the stale workspace cookie is dropped. `quote` makes the project slug safe inside the URL.
Non-browser clients (API calls, fetches) get a 409 with a machine-readable `code`, since a redirect would be useless to them.

A 404 or 409 may mean that the workspace was stopped by the idle reaper. `_idle_timeout_response` checks that and turns it into the idle-specific response; otherwise the original exception is re-raised unchanged.
Same path pattern as the HTTP catch-all but registered for WebSocket. The `with SessionLocal()` block makes sure the session is closed even if the proxy raises.

app/migrations.py.summary: Idempotent startup migrations that bring older databases up to the current schema without a migration framework. They add the role and OIDC columns to `users`, drop an obsolete workspace constraint, and create the partial unique index that allows only one active workspace per user and project. It supports PostgreSQL (production) and SQLite and skips other dialects with a warning.

notes.text: Names of the legacy constraint and the two partial unique indexes this module manages. They are interpolated into DDL strings and should match the index names declared in `app/models.py`.
Skips the migration when there is no `users` table yet. A fresh database is created from the models, so there is nothing to upgrade.

import logging

from sqlalchemy import inspect, text

from .db import engine

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

LEGACY_CONSTRAINT = "uq_activeish_workspace"
ACTIVE_INDEX = "uq_active_workspace"
OIDC_INDEX = "uq_oidc_identity"


def migrate_user_auth_schema() -> None:
    """Upgrade v6.5 and older users tables for roles and generic OIDC.

    Production uses PostgreSQL, where password_hash is made nullable for OIDC-only
    accounts. Fresh SQLite databases are created directly from the current model;
    legacy SQLite receives additive columns but keeps its historic NOT NULL rule.
    """
    inspector = inspect(engine)
    if "users" not in inspector.get_table_names():
        return

    dialect = engine.dialect.name
    with engine.begin() as conn:
        if dialect == "postgresql":
            statements = [
                "ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS role VARCHAR(20)",
                "ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS auth_provider VARCHAR(20)",
                "ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS oidc_issuer VARCHAR(512)",
                "ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS oidc_subject VARCHAR(512)",
                "ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS email VARCHAR(320)",
                "ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS display_name VARCHAR(160)",
                "ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS last_login_at TIMESTAMPTZ",
                "ALTER TABLE users ALTER COLUMN password_hash DROP NOT NULL",
            ]
            for statement in statements:
                conn.exec_driver_sql(statement)
        elif dialect == "sqlite":
            existing = {col["name"] for col in inspect(conn).get_columns("users")}
            additions = {
                "role": "VARCHAR(20)",
                "auth_provider": "VARCHAR(20)",
                "oidc_issuer": "VARCHAR(512)",
                "oidc_subject": "VARCHAR(512)",
                "email": "VARCHAR(320)",
                "display_name": "VARCHAR(160)",
                "last_login_at": "TIMESTAMP",
            }
            for name, sql_type in additions.items():
                if name not in existing:
                    conn.exec_driver_sql(f"ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN {name} {sql_type}")
        else:
            logger.warning("Unsupported dialect %s; user auth schema migration skipped", dialect)
            return

        conn.execute(text("UPDATE users SET role='developer' WHERE role IS NULL OR role=''"))
        conn.execute(text("UPDATE users SET auth_provider='local' WHERE auth_provider IS NULL OR auth_provider=''"))
        conn.execute(
            text(
                """UPDATE users SET role='admin'
                   WHERE id = (SELECT id FROM users ORDER BY created_at ASC, id ASC LIMIT 1)
                     AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM users WHERE role='admin')"""
            )
        )
        if dialect == "postgresql":
            conn.exec_driver_sql("ALTER TABLE users ALTER COLUMN role SET DEFAULT 'developer'")
            conn.exec_driver_sql("ALTER TABLE users ALTER COLUMN role SET NOT NULL")
            conn.exec_driver_sql("ALTER TABLE users ALTER COLUMN auth_provider SET DEFAULT 'local'")
            conn.exec_driver_sql("ALTER TABLE users ALTER COLUMN auth_provider SET NOT NULL")

        conn.execute(
            text(
                f'''CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "{OIDC_INDEX}"
                    ON users (oidc_issuer, oidc_subject)
                    WHERE oidc_subject IS NOT NULL'''
            )
        )
    logger.info("User auth schema is ready for local roles and OIDC")


def drop_legacy_workspace_constraint() -> None:
    dialect = engine.dialect.name
    if dialect == "postgresql":
        with engine.begin() as conn:
            conn.exec_driver_sql(
                f'ALTER TABLE IF EXISTS workspaces DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS "{LEGACY_CONSTRAINT}"'
            )
        logger.info("Dropped legacy workspace constraint if present: %s", LEGACY_CONSTRAINT)
    elif dialect == "sqlite":
        logger.info("SQLite detected; skipping in-place legacy constraint drop")


def ensure_active_workspace_index() -> None:
    dialect = engine.dialect.name
    if dialect not in {"postgresql", "sqlite"}:
        logger.warning("Unsupported dialect %s; active workspace index not created", dialect)
        return

    with engine.begin() as conn:
        conn.execute(
            text(
                f'''CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "{ACTIVE_INDEX}"
                    ON workspaces (user_id, project_slug)
                    WHERE status IN ('STARTING','RUNNING','STOPPING')'''
            )
        )
    logger.info("Ensured partial active-workspace index: %s", ACTIVE_INDEX)

notes.text: Values are lowercase strings, but SQLAlchemy `Enum` persists the member names by default, so the stored values are uppercase. This explains the uppercase literals in the index predicates at lines 68-69.

A partial unique index, declared for both PostgreSQL and SQLite via `postgresql_where` and `sqlite_where`. It guarantees one user row per OIDC identity while ignoring local accounts that have no subject.
The UUID default is a lambda so each new row gets its own value at insert time.
Nullable so OIDC-provisioned users can exist without a local password.
Passes the callable `now_utc` and does not call it. It is evaluated for each insert.
`in_use` is indexed, presumably so free slots can be found quickly. The code here does not show the lookup itself.
The partial index enforces at most one active workspace per user and project. Only workspaces in the STARTING, RUNNING or STOPPING states count.
Relationships with no `back_populates`, so they are one-directional: a workspace can reach its user and slot, but not the reverse.

app/oidc.py.summary: Generic OpenID Connect support built on Authlib. It registers one OIDC client from settings and maps provider claims to local `User` rows, creating the user on first login if auto-provisioning is enabled. If Authlib is not installed, the module still imports and OIDC requests fail with HTTP 503, so local-only deployments keep working.

notes.text: Authlib is optional. If the import fails, `OAuth` is `None` and `oauth` is `None`, so only OIDC features are unavailable.
Module-level registry and a flag recording whether the client has been registered.
PKCE is enabled by requesting the `S256` code challenge method on the client.
`or None` turns an empty secret into `None`, which is what a public (secret-less) client needs.
Picks the first non-empty candidate claim, takes the local part of an email, replaces unsafe characters, and truncates to 64 characters. Truncating leaves room for the suffix in `_unique_username`.
A deterministic hash of the identity makes the fallback username stable. `max(1, 80 - len(suffix) - 1)` leaves room for the suffix and the dash within the 80-character column.
Strips the trailing slash so the same issuer always matches the stored value.
Login for a known identity. Disabled accounts are refused, and profile fields are synced from the provider on every login.
Unknown users are rejected unless auto-provisioning is enabled.
Uses the shared first-user rule, so the first account in the system becomes an administrator even when it comes from OIDC.
OIDC accounts have no local password, which is why `password_hash` is nullable.
Handles the race between two simultaneous first logins. The loser's insert violates the unique identity index, so it rolls back and returns the row the other request created.

import hashlib
import re
from typing import Mapping, Any

try:
    from authlib.integrations.starlette_client import OAuth
except ImportError:  # Local-only deployments can still start if OIDC deps are absent.
    OAuth = None
from fastapi import HTTPException
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from .config import settings
from .models import User, UserRole
from .security import role_for_new_user


oauth = OAuth() if OAuth is not None else None
_oidc_registered = False


def configure_oidc() -> None:
    global _oidc_registered
    if not settings.oidc_configured:
        return
    if oauth is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail="OIDC support is not installed")
    if _oidc_registered:
        return
    client_kwargs = {"scope": settings.oidc_scopes}
    if settings.oidc_use_pkce:
        client_kwargs["code_challenge_method"] = "S256"
    oauth.register(
        name="generic_oidc",
        client_id=settings.oidc_client_id,
        client_secret=settings.oidc_client_secret or None,
        server_metadata_url=settings.effective_oidc_discovery_url,
        client_kwargs=client_kwargs,
    )
    _oidc_registered = True


def oidc_client():
    if not settings.oidc_configured:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="OIDC authentication is not configured")
    configure_oidc()
    if oauth is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail="OIDC support is not installed")
    client = oauth.create_client("generic_oidc")
    if client is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail="OIDC client is unavailable")
    return client


def _claim(userinfo: Mapping[str, Any], name: str) -> str | None:
    value = userinfo.get(name)
    if value is None:
        return None
    value = str(value).strip()
    return value or None


def _username_base(userinfo: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str:
    candidates = [
        _claim(userinfo, settings.oidc_username_claim),
        _claim(userinfo, settings.oidc_email_claim),
        _claim(userinfo, settings.oidc_name_claim),
        _claim(userinfo, "sub"),
    ]
    value = next((v for v in candidates if v), "oidc-user")
    if "@" in value:
        value = value.split("@", 1)[0]
    value = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]+", "-", value).strip("-._") or "oidc-user"
    return value[:64]


def _unique_username(db: Session, userinfo: Mapping[str, Any], issuer: str, subject: str) -> str:
    base = _username_base(userinfo)
    if db.scalar(select(User.id).where(User.username == base)) is None:
        return base
    suffix = hashlib.sha256(f"{issuer}|{subject}".encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
    max_base = max(1, 80 - len(suffix) - 1)
    return f"{base[:max_base]}-{suffix}"


def provision_oidc_user(db: Session, userinfo: Mapping[str, Any]) -> User:
    subject = _claim(userinfo, "sub")
    if not subject:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=502, detail="OIDC provider did not return a subject identifier")
    issuer = settings.oidc_issuer.rstrip("/")

    user = db.scalar(
        select(User).where(User.oidc_issuer == issuer, User.oidc_subject == subject)
    )
    if user:
        if not user.is_active:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="User account is disabled")
        user.email = _claim(userinfo, settings.oidc_email_claim)
        user.display_name = _claim(userinfo, settings.oidc_name_claim)
        db.commit()
        return user

    if not settings.oidc_auto_provision:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="OIDC user is not provisioned for this portal")

    role = role_for_new_user(db, settings.oidc_default_role)
    user = User(
        username=_unique_username(db, userinfo, issuer, subject),
        password_hash=None,
        role=role,
        auth_provider="oidc",
        oidc_issuer=issuer,
        oidc_subject=subject,
        email=_claim(userinfo, settings.oidc_email_claim),
        display_name=_claim(userinfo, settings.oidc_name_claim),
    )
    db.add(user)
    try:
        db.commit()
    except IntegrityError as exc:
        db.rollback()
        # A concurrent callback may have inserted this identity first.
        existing = db.scalar(
            select(User).where(User.oidc_issuer == issuer, User.oidc_subject == subject)
        )
        if existing:
            return existing
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail="Unable to provision OIDC account") from exc
    db.refresh(user)
    return user

app/opencode_update.py.summary: Implements the admin-triggered OpenCode engine update. It builds a candidate workspace image with Podman, smoke-tests it, then retags it as the live workspace image and records the new version in the control-plane env file. Progress lives in a process-wide state object guarded by a lock, which the portal can poll.

notes.text: Accepts `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` with optional pre-release and build metadata. This is the only gate on what reaches the `podman build` arguments and the env file.
A bounded deque keeps the log from growing without limit. Only the last 80 lines are retained.
`running` is derived from the status, so the UI does not need to know which states count as in progress.
Streaming mode merges stderr into stdout so one reader sees everything in order. Each line goes to `_append`, so the portal can show live build progress.
`wait(timeout)` runs only after stdout is exhausted. A command that keeps producing output indefinitely would never reach it.
Takes the last non-empty output line and extracts a semantic version from it, tolerating a prefix. It falls back to the raw text if no version matches.
Rewrites the env file line by line, replacing an existing `OPENCODE_VERSION=` entry or appending one, then restricts the file to owner-only access.
Updates the live `settings` object so the new version is used without a restart.
`+` is not valid in an image tag, so build metadata is converted to `_`.
Smoke test: the candidate must report exactly the requested version, or the update aborts before the live image is touched.
Activation: the live tag is repointed only now. `_persist_version` then records the choice so it survives restarts.
Failures are recorded in `_STATE` and not re-raised, because this runs in a background thread. The candidate image is kept for diagnosis.
Ensures `previous_version` is filled even when the update fails early.
Check-then-set under one lock hold, so only one update can be queued at a time.
A daemon thread keeps the HTTP request from blocking on the long build.

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import subprocess
import threading
from collections import deque
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import httpx

from .config import settings

_SEMVER = re.compile(r"^\d+\.\d+\.\d+(?:-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?(?:\+[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$")
_LOCK = threading.Lock()
_PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
_CONFIG_FILE = Path.home() / ".config" / "opencode-multiuser" / "control-plane.env"


def _now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()


@dataclass
class OpenCodeUpdateState:
    status: str = "idle"
    requested_version: str | None = None
    previous_version: str | None = None
    started_at: str | None = None
    finished_at: str | None = None
    message: str = "No update is running."
    error: str | None = None
    log_tail: deque[str] = field(default_factory=lambda: deque(maxlen=80))

    def payload(self) -> dict:
        data = asdict(self)
        data["log_tail"] = list(self.log_tail)
        data["running"] = self.status in {"queued", "building", "testing", "activating"}
        return data


_STATE = OpenCodeUpdateState()


def validate_version(version: str) -> str:
    value = version.strip()
    if not _SEMVER.fullmatch(value):
        raise ValueError("OpenCode version must be a semantic version such as 1.18.30")
    return value


def _append(message: str) -> None:
    with _LOCK:
        _STATE.log_tail.append(message.rstrip())
        _STATE.message = message.rstrip()


def _run(args: list[str], *, timeout: int = 900, stream: bool = False) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
    if not stream:
        cp = subprocess.run(args, text=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, timeout=timeout, check=False)
        if cp.returncode != 0:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"Command failed ({cp.returncode}): {' '.join(args)}\n"
                f"stdout:\n{cp.stdout[-4000:]}\nstderr:\n{cp.stderr[-4000:]}"
            )
        return cp

    proc = subprocess.Popen(args, text=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    output: list[str] = []
    try:
        assert proc.stdout is not None
        for line in proc.stdout:
            output.append(line)
            _append(line.strip())
        rc = proc.wait(timeout=timeout)
    except Exception:
        proc.kill()
        raise
    text = "".join(output)
    if rc != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Command failed ({rc}): {' '.join(args)}\n{text[-8000:]}")
    return subprocess.CompletedProcess(args, rc, stdout=text, stderr="")


def configured_version() -> str:
    return settings.opencode_version


def installed_version() -> str | None:
    try:
        cp = _run(
            [settings.podman_bin, "run", "--rm", settings.workspace_image, "--version"],
            timeout=60,
        )
    except Exception:
        return None
    value = cp.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1].strip() if cp.stdout.strip() else ""
    # OpenCode currently prints the bare semantic version. Be tolerant of a prefix.
    match = re.search(r"\d+\.\d+\.\d+(?:-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?", value)
    return match.group(0) if match else (value or None)


def latest_version() -> str:
    response = httpx.get(settings.opencode_registry_url, timeout=10.0, follow_redirects=True)
    response.raise_for_status()
    payload = response.json()
    version = payload.get("version")
    if not isinstance(version, str):
        raise RuntimeError("OpenCode registry response did not contain a version")
    return validate_version(version)


def _persist_version(version: str) -> None:
    _CONFIG_FILE.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    lines = _CONFIG_FILE.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if _CONFIG_FILE.exists() else []
    replaced = False
    output: list[str] = []
    for line in lines:
        if line.startswith("OPENCODE_VERSION="):
            output.append(f"OPENCODE_VERSION={version}")
            replaced = True
        else:
            output.append(line)
    if not replaced:
        output.append(f"OPENCODE_VERSION={version}")
    _CONFIG_FILE.write_text("\n".join(output) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    _CONFIG_FILE.chmod(0o600)
    settings.opencode_version = version


def _perform_update(version: str) -> None:
    safe_tag = version.replace("+", "_")
    candidate = f"localhost/opencode-workspace:{safe_tag}"
    previous = configured_version()
    try:
        with _LOCK:
            _STATE.status = "building"
            _STATE.message = f"Building OpenCode {version} candidate image…"
        _append(f"Building candidate image {candidate}")
        _run(
            [
                settings.podman_bin,
                "build",
                "--build-arg",
                f"OPENCODE_VERSION={version}",
                "-t",
                candidate,
                "-f",
                str(_PROJECT_ROOT / "Containerfile.workspace"),
                str(_PROJECT_ROOT),
            ],
            timeout=settings.opencode_update_timeout_seconds,
            stream=True,
        )

        with _LOCK:
            _STATE.status = "testing"
            _STATE.message = "Smoke-testing the candidate image…"
        cp = _run([settings.podman_bin, "run", "--rm", candidate, "--version"], timeout=60)
        reported = cp.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1].strip() if cp.stdout.strip() else ""
        match = re.search(r"\d+\.\d+\.\d+(?:-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?", reported)
        actual = match.group(0) if match else reported
        if actual != version:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Candidate image reported OpenCode {actual!r}; expected {version!r}")
        _append(f"Smoke test passed: OpenCode {actual}")

        with _LOCK:
            _STATE.status = "activating"
            _STATE.message = "Activating the tested image…"
        _run([settings.podman_bin, "tag", candidate, settings.workspace_image], timeout=60)
        _persist_version(version)
        _append(f"Activated {settings.workspace_image} -> OpenCode {version}")
        _append("Existing running workspaces are unchanged; restart them to use the new image.")

        with _LOCK:
            _STATE.status = "success"
            _STATE.finished_at = _now()
            _STATE.message = f"OpenCode {version} is active for newly started workspaces."
            _STATE.error = None
    except Exception as exc:
        with _LOCK:
            _STATE.status = "error"
            _STATE.finished_at = _now()
            _STATE.message = "OpenCode update failed. The previous latest image was left unchanged."
            _STATE.error = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
        _append(f"ERROR: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
        # Keep the candidate tag for diagnosis/possible manual inspection.
    finally:
        with _LOCK:
            if _STATE.previous_version is None:
                _STATE.previous_version = previous


def start_update(version: str) -> dict:
    version = validate_version(version)
    with _LOCK:
        if _STATE.status in {"queued", "building", "testing", "activating"}:
            raise RuntimeError("An OpenCode update is already running")
        _STATE.status = "queued"
        _STATE.requested_version = version
        _STATE.previous_version = configured_version()
        _STATE.started_at = _now()
        _STATE.finished_at = None
        _STATE.message = f"Queued OpenCode {version} update."
        _STATE.error = None
        _STATE.log_tail.clear()
    thread = threading.Thread(target=_perform_update, args=(version,), name="opencode-image-update", daemon=True)
    thread.start()
    return update_status()


def update_status() -> dict:
    with _LOCK:
        return _STATE.payload()


def system_snapshot(*, check_latest: bool = False) -> dict:
    latest: str | None = None
    latest_error: str | None = None
    if check_latest:
        try:
            latest = latest_version()
        except Exception as exc:
            latest_error = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
    return {
        "configured_version": configured_version(),
        "installed_version": installed_version(),
        "latest_version": latest,
        "latest_error": latest_error,
        "workspace_image": settings.workspace_image,
        "registry_url": settings.opencode_registry_url,
        "update": update_status(),
    }

app/portal.py.summary: Defines the small management widget that the gateway injects into OpenCode's own HTML pages. It holds the widget's CSS and JavaScript as string constants, a function that builds its markup, and a function that inserts that markup into an HTML document. The widget offers Dashboard, Stop workspace and Logout actions, and the script polls a status endpoint to send the user back to the dashboard when the workspace is no longer running.

notes.text: `PORTAL_CSS` is scoped under `#oc-mu-portal` so it cannot clash with OpenCode's own styles, and includes a dark-mode variant and a busy state that disables interaction.
Guard against running twice: it exits if the widget is missing or already marked as bound through `data-bound`.
Waits two animation frames before submitting so the browser paints the busy state first. Otherwise the navigation could start before the user sees any feedback.
The default link/form behaviour is intercepted only to add the busy state and, for Stop and Logout, a confirmation prompt. The underlying link and forms still work if the script does not run.
Polls `/_portal/status` with the session cookie and no caching. A 401 means the session ended, so the user is sent to `/login`. Other non-OK responses are ignored.
If the workspace was stopped for inactivity, redirect to the dashboard with `reason=idle` and the project slug so the dashboard can explain what happened.
Any non-running state sends the user back to `/dashboard`.
Errors are swallowed on purpose: a transient network or gateway failure must not disrupt the OpenCode page the user is working in.
Status is checked every 30 seconds.
The slug is escaped with `quote=True` because it is interpolated into an HTML attribute and into text.
The widget is a `<details>`/`<summary>` element, so opening and closing the menu works without JavaScript.
Stylesheet and script are loaded from `/_portal/` URLs instead of being inlined.
Idempotence check on the widget's id.
Case-insensitive search for the last `</body>`. The widget is inserted before it, and appended at the end when no closing tag exists.

app/runtime.py.summary: Wraps the Podman CLI and the on-disk layout that make up a workspace runtime. It computes per-user/per-project data directories, stores the per-workspace Basic Auth secret, activity timestamp and stop reason as small files, starts a locked-down OpenCode container bound to a loopback port derived from its slot, and polls it until healthy. The gateway and the control plane in `app/main.py` (not shown here) call these helpers.

notes.text: Whitelist for project slugs. Together with the explicit `.`/`..` check in `workspace_root` it keeps slugs from escaping the data directory.
`check=False` is passed to `subprocess.run` on purpose: the helper handles the exit code itself so the error message can include both streams. The 90 second timeout applies to every Podman call.
`.` and `..` consist only of allowed characters, so the regex alone would let them through. They are rejected separately.
Atomic publish: write JSON to a temp file in the same directory, chmod it to 0o644, then `replace` it into place. Same-directory temp files keep `replace` atomic.
Safety check before the recursive delete. The root must be directly under the user's directory and must not be a symlink.
Activity is derived from the file's mtime, converted to a UTC-aware datetime.
The stop reason file is restricted to the owner (0o600).
The secret is written first and restricted afterwards. It is the Basic Auth password the gateway injects for OpenCode.
A missing secret is treated as an upgrade condition. The error tells the user to restart the workspace so a runtime with a stored secret is created.
Basic Auth credential for the `opencode` user, matching `OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME` set in `start_workspace`.
Fail fast if the container has already exited, and include recent logs in the error instead of waiting out the full timeout.
Any 2xx counts as ready. Other statuses are retried and recorded for the final timeout message.
Transient connection problems are expected while OpenCode boots. They are recorded and retried, and the connection is always closed in `finally`.
The container name combines the slot with a 12-character id prefix, so a slot's container name changes with the workspace occupying it.
Clears leftovers from a previous crash: removes any container with the same name, drops the old stop reason, and stores the new secret before the container starts.
OpenCode is published only on `127.0.0.1` because the gateway runs as a native service on the same host. Container port 4096 maps to the slot's host port.
Hardening: memory, CPU and PID limits, no privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped, a read-only root filesystem and tmpfs for `/tmp` and the cache directory.
`keep-id` maps the container user (uid/gid 10001) onto the invoking host user in the rootless user namespace, so the bind-mounted data stays writable.
The four persistent directories are bind-mounted read-write. The `Z` option relabels them for SELinux.
The managed provider policy is mounted read-only so workspace users cannot change it.
Optional CORS setting is passed through only if configured.
If the container never becomes ready it is removed so it does not hold the slot's port and name, then the original exception propagates.
Go-template query on `podman inspect` that prints `true` or `false`.
Compares each line of `podman port` output to the expected `127.0.0.1:<port>` mapping.

app/runtime.py.text:
import base64
import http.client
import json
import re
import secrets
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from .config import settings

_SAFE = re.compile(r"^[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+$")


@dataclass
class RuntimeResult:
    container_name: str
    basic_password: str
    host_port: int


def _run(args: list[str], check: bool = True) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    cp = subprocess.run(
        [settings.podman_bin, *args],
        check=False,
        text=True,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
        timeout=90,
    )
    if check and cp.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Podman command failed with exit code {cp.returncode}\n"
            f"stdout:\n{cp.stdout}\n"
            f"stderr:\n{cp.stderr}"
        )
    return cp


def ensure_network() -> None:
    result = _run(["network", "exists", settings.podman_network], check=False)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        _run(["network", "create", settings.podman_network])


def workspace_root(user_id: str, project_slug: str) -> Path:
    if project_slug in {".", ".."} or not _SAFE.fullmatch(project_slug):
        raise ValueError("invalid project slug")
    return settings.expanded_data_root / "users" / user_id / project_slug


def workspace_paths(user_id: str, project_slug: str) -> tuple[Path, Path, Path, Path]:
    root = workspace_root(user_id, project_slug)
    workspace = root / "workspace"
    data = root / "opencode-data"
    state = root / "opencode-state"
    config = root / "opencode-config"
    for path in (workspace, data, state, config):
        path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return workspace, data, state, config


def managed_opencode_config_path() -> Path | None:
    """Write the administrator provider policy as immutable OpenCode settings."""
    policy: dict[str, list[str] | str] = {
        "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
    }
    if settings.enabled_provider_ids:
        policy["enabled_providers"] = settings.enabled_provider_ids
    if settings.disabled_provider_ids:
        policy["disabled_providers"] = settings.disabled_provider_ids
    if len(policy) == 1:
        return None

    policy_dir = settings.expanded_data_root / "policy"
    policy_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = policy_dir / "opencode.json"
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(
        mode="w", encoding="utf-8", dir=policy_dir, prefix=".opencode.", delete=False
    ) as output:
        json.dump(policy, output, sort_keys=True)
        output.write("\n")
        temporary_path = Path(output.name)
    temporary_path.chmod(0o644)
    temporary_path.replace(path)
    return path


def remove_workspace_data(user_id: str, project_slug: str) -> None:
    """Permanently remove one workspace's project and OpenCode state."""
    root = workspace_root(user_id, project_slug)
    user_root = settings.expanded_data_root / "users" / user_id
    if root.parent != user_root or root.is_symlink():
        raise ValueError("unsafe workspace data path")
    if root.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(root)



def workspace_activity_path(user_id: str, project_slug: str) -> Path:
    return workspace_root(user_id, project_slug) / "last-activity"


def touch_workspace_activity(user_id: str, project_slug: str) -> None:
    path = workspace_activity_path(user_id, project_slug)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.touch(exist_ok=True)


def workspace_last_activity(user_id: str, project_slug: str) -> datetime | None:
    path = workspace_activity_path(user_id, project_slug)
    if not path.exists():
        return None
    return datetime.fromtimestamp(path.stat().st_mtime, tz=timezone.utc)


def workspace_secret_path(user_id: str, project_slug: str) -> Path:
    return workspace_root(user_id, project_slug) / "runtime-secret"


def workspace_stop_reason_path(user_id: str, project_slug: str) -> Path:
    return workspace_root(user_id, project_slug) / "stop-reason"


def write_workspace_stop_reason(user_id: str, project_slug: str, reason: str) -> None:
    path = workspace_stop_reason_path(user_id, project_slug)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(reason.strip() + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    path.chmod(0o600)


def read_workspace_stop_reason(user_id: str, project_slug: str) -> str | None:
    path = workspace_stop_reason_path(user_id, project_slug)
    if not path.is_file():
        return None
    value = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
    return value or None


def clear_workspace_stop_reason(user_id: str, project_slug: str) -> None:
    workspace_stop_reason_path(user_id, project_slug).unlink(missing_ok=True)


def write_workspace_secret(user_id: str, project_slug: str, password: str) -> None:
    path = workspace_secret_path(user_id, project_slug)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(password, encoding="utf-8")
    path.chmod(0o600)


def read_workspace_secret(user_id: str, project_slug: str) -> str:
    path = workspace_secret_path(user_id, project_slug)
    if not path.is_file():
        raise RuntimeError(
            "Workspace runtime secret is missing. Stop and restart this workspace "
            "so it is recreated by the gateway-enabled runtime."
        )
    return path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()


def workspace_host_port(slot_id: int) -> int:
    return settings.workspace_host_port_base + slot_id



def wait_workspace_ready(container_name: str, host_port: int, password: str) -> None:
    deadline = time.monotonic() + settings.workspace_ready_timeout_seconds
    credentials = base64.b64encode(f"opencode:{password}".encode("utf-8")).decode("ascii")
    last_error = "backend has not accepted a connection yet"

    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        if not container_running(container_name):
            logs = _run(["logs", "--tail", "80", container_name], check=False)
            detail = (logs.stderr or logs.stdout or "no container logs available").strip()
            raise RuntimeError(f"OpenCode container exited before becoming ready: {detail}")

        connection = None
        try:
            connection = http.client.HTTPConnection("127.0.0.1", host_port, timeout=2)
            connection.request(
                "GET",
                "/global/health",
                headers={"Authorization": f"Basic {credentials}"},
            )
            response = connection.getresponse()
            response.read()
            if 200 <= response.status < 300:
                return
            last_error = f"health endpoint returned HTTP {response.status}"
        except (TimeoutError, OSError, http.client.HTTPException) as exc:
            last_error = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
        finally:
            if connection is not None:
                connection.close()

        time.sleep(settings.workspace_ready_poll_interval_seconds)

    raise RuntimeError(
        f"OpenCode did not become ready within {settings.workspace_ready_timeout_seconds}s "
        f"on 127.0.0.1:{host_port} ({last_error})"
    )


def start_workspace(user_id: str, project_slug: str, workspace_id: str, slot_id: int) -> RuntimeResult:
    ensure_network()
    workspace, data, state, config = workspace_paths(user_id, project_slug)
    managed_config = managed_opencode_config_path()
    short = workspace_id.replace("-", "")[:12]
    container_name = f"oc-{slot_id}-{short}"
    password = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
    host_port = workspace_host_port(slot_id)

    # Defensive cleanup in case a prior crash left the slot's name behind.
    _run(["rm", "-f", container_name], check=False)
    clear_workspace_stop_reason(user_id, project_slug)
    write_workspace_secret(user_id, project_slug, password)

    args = [
        "run", "-d",
        "--name", container_name,
        "--network", settings.podman_network,
        # The gateway is a native user service, so expose OpenCode only on
        # loopback. Nothing outside the host can connect directly to this port.
        "--publish", f"127.0.0.1:{host_port}:4096",
        "--memory", settings.workspace_memory,
        "--cpus", str(settings.workspace_cpus),
        "--pids-limit", str(settings.workspace_pids_limit),
        "--security-opt", "no-new-privileges",
        "--cap-drop", "ALL",
        "--userns", "keep-id:uid=10001,gid=10001",
        "--read-only",
        "--tmpfs", "/tmp:rw,nosuid,nodev,size=1g,mode=1777",
        "--tmpfs", "/home/opencode/.cache:rw,nosuid,nodev,size=512m,mode=1777",
        "--volume", f"{workspace}:/workspace:rw,Z",
        "--volume", f"{data}:/home/opencode/.local/share/opencode:rw,Z",
        "--volume", f"{state}:/home/opencode/.local/state:rw,Z",
        "--volume", f"{config}:/home/opencode/.config/opencode:rw,Z",
        "--env", "HOME=/home/opencode",
        "--env", "XDG_DATA_HOME=/home/opencode/.local/share",
        "--env", "XDG_STATE_HOME=/home/opencode/.local/state",
        "--env", "XDG_CACHE_HOME=/home/opencode/.cache",
        "--env", "XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/home/opencode/.config",
        "--env", "OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME=opencode",
        "--env", f"OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD={password}",
    ]
    if managed_config is not None:
        args.extend([
            "--volume", f"{managed_config}:/etc/opencode/opencode.json:ro,Z",
        ])
    if settings.opencode_cors:
        args.extend(["--env", f"OPENCODE_CORS={settings.opencode_cors}"])
    args.extend([
        settings.workspace_image,
        "serve", "--hostname", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "4096"
    ])
    _run(args)
    try:
        wait_workspace_ready(container_name, host_port, password)
    except Exception:
        _run(["rm", "-f", container_name], check=False)
        raise
    touch_workspace_activity(user_id, project_slug)
    return RuntimeResult(container_name=container_name, basic_password=password, host_port=host_port)


def stop_workspace(container_name: str | None) -> None:
    if not container_name:
        return
    _run(["rm", "-f", container_name], check=False)


def container_running(container_name: str | None) -> bool:
    if not container_name:
        return False
    cp = _run(["inspect", "-f", "{{.State.Running}}", container_name], check=False)
    return cp.returncode == 0 and cp.stdout.strip() == "true"


def container_has_workspace_port(container_name: str | None, slot_id: int | None) -> bool:
    """Return True when the runtime exposes slot's expected loopback port."""
    if not container_name or slot_id is None:
        return False
    cp = _run(["port", container_name, "4096/tcp"], check=False)
    if cp.returncode != 0:
        return False
    expected = f"127.0.0.1:{workspace_host_port(slot_id)}"
    return any(line.strip() == expected for line in cp.stdout.splitlines())

app/schemas.py.summary: Pydantic request and response models for the HTTP API: registration and login, token responses, workspace start and info, admin user updates and the OpenCode engine update request. Field constraints validate input at the API boundary.

notes.text: Username and password limits are enforced by pydantic on input, so invalid requests are rejected before any handler logic runs.
The anchored regex limits `role` to exactly `admin` or `developer`.
The regex is semver: `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, then an optional `-prerelease` and an optional `+build` part. No leading `v` is accepted.

app/security.py.summary: Authentication and authorization helpers for the control plane. It covers Argon2 password hashing, issuing and verifying HS256 JWT session tokens, resolving the current user from a bearer token or session cookie, and the first-user-becomes-admin rule. `current_user` and `require_admin` are FastAPI dependencies that protect routes.

notes.text: `auto_error=False` stops FastAPI from returning 401 when there is no `Authorization` header, so `current_user` can fall back to the session cookie.
Accounts with no local password hash, such as OIDC users, can never pass password verification.
On PostgreSQL, takes a table lock before counting users. `SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE` conflicts with itself, so concurrent first registrations are serialized, and the lock lasts until the transaction ends.
The first account becomes the administrator. Later accounts get `default_role`, but only if it is a known role, so a misconfigured default falls back to `developer`.
Claims: `sub` is the user id, `usr` and `role` are informational, and `exp` bounds the token's lifetime.
Pins the accepted algorithm to HS256 and treats any failure, including signature, expiry and a missing `sub`, as unauthenticated.
Re-checks the database on every request, so a disabled or deleted user loses access even with an unexpired token.
Bearer header first, then the session cookie. The cookie is how the browser portal stays authenticated.
Authorization uses the role on the current database row, not the role claim in the token.

app/traefik.py.summary: Small helpers for the Traefik side of the platform: building the public URL used to open a workspace and removing leftover per-workspace Traefik route files from an older design.

notes.text: Uses `rstrip('/')` so the result has exactly one slash before `open`, whether or not the configured URL ends in a slash.
The docstring says these are v5 per-workspace route files, which v6 no longer uses.
Early return makes the cleanup a no-op when the directory does not exist.
Only `workspace-*.yml` files are removed. `missing_ok=True` keeps this safe against a concurrent or repeated deletion.

app/ui.py.summary: Server-rendered HTML for the portal's own pages: login, registration, the workspace dashboard, the admin user console and the admin system console. Each page is one Python f-string with its JavaScript inline, and all of them share the `APP_CSS` stylesheet and the inline SVG icons from `_icon`. The pages are static shells. They fetch data from the portal's JSON endpoints (for example `/workspaces`, `/api/admin/users`) after loading.

notes.text: `APP_CSS` is a raw string, so CSS backslashes and braces are kept literally. The pages link to it as `/_ui/app.css`.
Unknown icon names fall back to the `code` icon. The class is added by rewriting the opening `<svg ` tag.
Only known error codes produce a notice, and the text shown is a fixed message rather than the raw value, which avoids reflecting user input.
The Register link appears only if local auth is on and registration is enabled.
The divider appears only when both login methods are on, and the delegation note only when SSO is the sole method.
`local_script` is a raw (non-f) string, so its braces are written normally. It is inserted into the page template through `{local_script}`.

Login flow: validate the form, post JSON to `/auth/login`, use the server's `detail` string as the error message if it is one, and otherwise go to `/dashboard`. On failure the button is restored and the password field is focused.
The whole page is one f-string. The version shown comes from `__version__` and is escaped.
The note changes with `first_user`. The first account is announced as the bootstrap administrator.
Inside this f-string the inline script's braces are doubled (`{{`, `}}`) so they render as single braces. The script checks password equality before calling `/auth/register`.
Username and role are escaped and the initials are derived from the display name, falling back to the username. The Admin link is added only for the `admin` role.
`notice_html` is inserted unescaped, so it must come from trusted code.
The free slot count starts with the server value and is refreshed by the script from `/_portal/overview`.
Skeleton placeholders are shown until the first `refresh()` replaces them with workspace cards.
Client-side HTML escaper used before API data goes into `innerHTML` templates.
`setBusy` shows the overlay and disables every button, and can cycle through staged messages every 1.7 seconds. These are cosmetic and not tied to real progress. `hideBusy` undoes both.
`api` wrapper that sends cookies, turns a non-OK response into an `Error` carrying the server's `detail`, and returns `null` for 204.

Card actions depend on state. A running workspace with a `url` gets Open and Stop, a running one without a `url` is treated as legacy and gets Upgrade runtime, and stopped or errored ones get Start. Remove is always present.
`refresh` loads `/workspaces`, updates counts and cards, then tries `/_portal/overview` for free slots. A failure of the overview call is deliberately ignored.
Starting a workspace shows staged messages and navigates to the returned `url` when the API call completes. On failure the overlay is hidden and the list is refreshed.
Stop and Remove go through confirmation dialogs first. Removal calls `DELETE /workspaces/<id>` and the text states that the data is permanently deleted.
Logout posts to `/logout`, whose text says it stops active workspaces, and then goes to `/login`.
Display name and initials are escaped and fall back to the username.

Row rendering decides which actions are available. A user cannot change their own role or status, password reset is for `local` accounts only, Stop appears only when active workspaces exist, and Delete appears only if `can_delete` is true.
Search and role/status filters run in the browser over the already loaded `users` array.
Admin actions call per-user endpoints. After a rejection the page refreshes so the controls match the server state again.
The client requires at least 12 characters before calling the reset endpoint.
Deletion is limited by the dialog text to accounts with no workspace history. The server decides through `can_delete`.

`renderUpdate` shows status and log, disables the buttons while an update is running and starts or stops a 1.2 second poller. A transition from a non-success state to `success` triggers a reload of system info.
Loads portal and OpenCode info, and prefills the target version field only if it is empty so a user's edit is not overwritten.

The version is validated client-side as semantic version (`x.y.z` with optional pre-release and build parts). The doubled backslashes are Python string escaping of the JavaScript regular expression. The user must confirm before the update is posted.

app/version.py.summary: Holds the application version as a single `__version__` string. Its docstring declares it the single source of truth for the Semantic Versioning number, and `app/__init__.py` re-exports it.

notes.text: The version literal itself, in MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH form. The docstring says to inspect or update it with `python3 scripts/version.py` instead of editing it by hand.
