OpenCode Multiuser follows Semantic Versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH).
This module is the single source of truth for the application version.
Use ``python3 scripts/version.py`` to inspect or update it.
"""

__version__ = "0.11.2"

scripts/check-host.sh.summary: A read-only diagnostic that prints whether the current Linux user has what rootless Podman needs under systemd: a runtime directory, a user D-Bus socket, delegated cgroup controllers, and Podman's own cgroup/runtime settings. It makes no changes. `install.sh` runs similar preflight checks and aborts on failure, while this script only reports.

notes.text: Uses `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` when set, otherwise the conventional `/run/user/<uid>` path that a systemd user session provides.

Path of the cgroup v2 file that lists the controllers systemd has delegated to this user's `user@<uid>.service` manager. Rootless Podman can only enforce CPU, memory and PID limits for controllers listed here.

The `[[ test ]] && echo OK || echo MISSING` idiom is safe under `set -e` because the test sits in an `&&`/`||` list. `bus` is tested with `-S` (is a socket), since `systemctl --user` needs that socket.

The controllers file is printed if readable. If not, the script reports 'unavailable' with the path instead of failing, because the path may not exist on hosts without cgroup v2 or without a user manager.
Asks Podman for cgroup version, cgroup manager and OCI runtime name. `2>/dev/null || true` hides errors and keeps the exit status 0, so a missing or broken Podman does not abort the report.

scripts/check-host.sh.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
uid=$(id -u)
runtime=${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/run/user/$uid}
controllers="/sys/fs/cgroup/user.slice/user-${uid}.slice/user@${uid}.service/cgroup.controllers"

echo "user: $(id -un) (uid=$uid)"
echo "runtime: $runtime"
[[ -d "$runtime" ]] && echo "runtime dir: OK" || echo "runtime dir: MISSING"
[[ -S "$runtime/bus" ]] && echo "user bus: OK" || echo "user bus: MISSING"
if [[ -r "$controllers" ]]; then
  echo "cgroup controllers: $(cat "$controllers")"
else
  echo "cgroup controllers: unavailable ($controllers)"
fi
podman info --format 'podman: cgroupVersion={{.Host.CgroupsVersion}} cgroupManager={{.Host.CgroupManager}} runtime={{.Host.OCIRuntime.Name}}' 2>/dev/null || true

scripts/install.sh.summary: Installer and upgrader for a single-user-account host. Run from an extracted release tree, it preflights Python, the systemd user session and cgroup delegation. It then copies the app to `~/opt/opencode-multiuser`, writes or migrates `control-plane.env`, renders the Quadlet and Traefik files, builds the Python venv and the workspace image, and starts the services. It is meant to be re-run for upgrades: settings already saved in `control-plane.env` are kept unless the matching variable is set explicitly in the environment.

notes.text: Each tunable follows the same pattern. If the variable was set in the caller's environment (`${VAR+x}` is non-empty even for an empty value), an `*_EXPLICIT` flag is recorded before the default is applied. Later code uses that flag to tell an explicit override from a default, so a re-run does not overwrite persisted settings with defaults. Only the variables with an `_EXPLICIT` flag take part in this persistence. `CONTROL_PLANE_BIND`, `TRAEFIK_PUBLIC_PORT`, `TRAEFIK_ENTRYPOINT` and `WORKSPACE_HOST_PORT_BASE` are plain defaults.
`SELF_DIR` is the repository root, one level above `scripts/`, and is the source tree that is copied to the install target.

Refuses to continue if key files (the portal, UI, OIDC and update modules, `app/version.py`, `uv.lock`) are missing. The comment says the aim is to prevent a partial upgrade from an incomplete extraction.

Picks the interpreter. `PYTHON_BIN` overrides the search; otherwise it tries `python3.13`, `python3.12`, `python3.11` and `python3`, and accepts the first one whose `sys.version_info` is at least 3.11. The result is stored as an absolute path from `command -v`.
Extracts `__version__` from `app/version.py` with `sed`, not by importing it, so no Python environment is needed yet. The script exits if nothing is found.
Points `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` at the user's systemd session. This allows `systemctl --user` to work in sessions such as `su` or `sudo -u` where these variables are not set.

Fails with remediation steps when the runtime directory or the D-Bus socket does not exist. The message says to enable linger and start the user manager as root, and not to create `/run/user/<uid>` by hand.
Checks that `systemctl --user` can actually talk to the user manager, since the socket existing does not prove that it works.

Preflight for rootless Podman resource limits. It reads the cgroup controllers delegated to the user manager and requires `cpu`, `memory` and `pids`. The leading and trailing spaces added around the list make the `*" $ctrl "*` test match whole words only. If the file cannot be read, it only warns.
Fixed per-user install locations for the app, config, Quadlet unit files and systemd user units.

On upgrade, reads previously saved values from `control-plane.env` for each variable that was not set explicitly. `tail -1` takes the last occurrence if a key appears more than once. The provider lists are copied even when empty, so an empty saved value is kept, while the other values are only restored if non-empty.

Expands a literal `%h` (the systemd home-directory specifier) to `$HOME`, applies defaults (the Traefik dynamic directory defaults to a folder under `DATA_ROOT`), and requires both paths to be absolute.

Stops the control-plane service first, so its port is free for the check. The check uses `ss` to see if anything is listening on `CONTROL_PLANE_PORT` and aborts with a suggested alternative if so. It is skipped when `ss` is not installed.

Mirrors the source tree into the install target with `--delete`, so files removed from the release also disappear from the install. `.venv` and `.pytest_cache` are excluded from both copy and deletion.
Rechecks that the same key files arrived in the target after the copy.

Installs the Quadlet unit files, then renders `traefik.container` by replacing the `__TRAEFIK_DYNAMIC_DIR__` and `__TRAEFIK_STATE_DIR__` placeholders. The `*_SED` values are first escaped for `&`, `|` and `\`, which are special in the `sed` replacement that uses `|` as the delimiter. It also installs the control-plane systemd unit and the Traefik static config.
Generates a Postgres password with `openssl rand` only the first time and stores it in a mode-600 file. Later runs reuse it, so the database password stays in step with the existing database.

Upgrade: leaves existing values alone and appends only keys that are missing (`grep -q '^KEY=' || echo ... >>`). This lets new settings added in later versions appear without overwriting administrator edits.
If `DATA_ROOT` or `TRAEFIK_DYNAMIC_DIR` was set explicitly, the saved line is replaced in place, or appended if absent, using the escaped `*_SED` value.

Rewrites `CONTROL_PLANE_URL` in two known upgrade cases: the old `http://code.example.com` default, and an `https://$BASE_DOMAIN` URL when `TRAEFIK_TLS` is not `true`. Custom URLs are left alone. The comment says the second case keeps cookies and `/open/<workspace>` redirects working on HTTP.
An explicit `OPENCODE_VERSION` from the environment replaces the saved version, or is appended if the key is missing. Without it the saved value stays in effect.

Same persistence for the two provider-policy variables, in a loop that reads the variable and its `_EXPLICIT` flag by indirect expansion (`${!name}`). Only `sed` metacharacters are escaped, since the values are comma-separated provider IDs.
Reads back the effective port and entrypoint from the saved file, falling back to the script values. This means templates use what the service will actually read.

Renders the Traefik dynamic route for the control plane from a template with placeholders. It then deletes old `workspace-*.yml` per-workspace routes, since the comment says v6 serves all workspaces through one gateway route.

Recreates the virtualenv from scratch each run, installs `pip` and `uv`, then runs `uv sync --frozen --no-dev` in the target directory. `--frozen` installs exactly what `uv.lock` lists and `--no-dev` leaves out dev dependencies.
Builds the workspace image with the effective OpenCode version as a build argument, then pulls the PostgreSQL 17 and Traefik v3.5 images.

Reloads systemd so it sees the new units, starts the network, Postgres and Traefik services, and waits 2 seconds. It then enables and restarts the control-plane service. The fixed `sleep 2` is only a delay and not a readiness check.
Prints a summary of the URLs, config path, auth defaults, OpenCode version and capacity model, along with a note that the control-plane port should be kept off untrusted networks.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

if [[ -n "${BASE_DOMAIN+x}" ]]; then BASE_DOMAIN_EXPLICIT=1; fi
BASE_DOMAIN=${BASE_DOMAIN:-code.example.com}
if [[ -n "${OPENCODE_VERSION+x}" ]]; then OPENCODE_VERSION_EXPLICIT=1; fi
OPENCODE_VERSION=${OPENCODE_VERSION:-1.18.30}
if [[ -n "${OPENCODE_ENABLED_PROVIDERS+x}" ]]; then OPENCODE_ENABLED_PROVIDERS_EXPLICIT=1; fi
OPENCODE_ENABLED_PROVIDERS=${OPENCODE_ENABLED_PROVIDERS:-}
if [[ -n "${OPENCODE_DISABLED_PROVIDERS+x}" ]]; then OPENCODE_DISABLED_PROVIDERS_EXPLICIT=1; fi
OPENCODE_DISABLED_PROVIDERS=${OPENCODE_DISABLED_PROVIDERS:-}
if [[ -n "${CONTROL_PLANE_PORT+x}" ]]; then CONTROL_PLANE_PORT_EXPLICIT=1; fi
CONTROL_PLANE_PORT=${CONTROL_PLANE_PORT:-8010}
if [[ -n "${DATA_ROOT+x}" ]]; then DATA_ROOT_EXPLICIT=1; fi
DATA_ROOT=${DATA_ROOT:-}
if [[ -n "${TRAEFIK_DYNAMIC_DIR+x}" ]]; then TRAEFIK_DYNAMIC_DIR_EXPLICIT=1; fi
TRAEFIK_DYNAMIC_DIR=${TRAEFIK_DYNAMIC_DIR:-}
CONTROL_PLANE_BIND=${CONTROL_PLANE_BIND:-0.0.0.0}
TRAEFIK_PUBLIC_PORT=${TRAEFIK_PUBLIC_PORT:-8443}
TRAEFIK_ENTRYPOINT=${TRAEFIK_ENTRYPOINT:-websecure}
WORKSPACE_HOST_PORT_BASE=${WORKSPACE_HOST_PORT_BASE:-41000}
SELF_DIR=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)

# v6.4+ requires the portal injection module. Refuse to perform a partial
# upgrade if the extracted source tree is incomplete.
for required_file in app/portal.py app/ui.py app/oidc.py app/opencode_update.py app/version.py uv.lock; do
  if [[ ! -f "$SELF_DIR/$required_file" ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: $SELF_DIR/$required_file is missing." >&2
    echo "Extract the complete release archive and run install.sh from that tree." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

if [[ -n "${PYTHON_BIN:-}" ]]; then
  PYTHON_CANDIDATES=("$PYTHON_BIN")
else
  PYTHON_CANDIDATES=(python3.13 python3.12 python3.11 python3)
fi

PYTHON_BIN=""
for candidate in "${PYTHON_CANDIDATES[@]}"; do
  if command -v "$candidate" >/dev/null 2>&1 && \
     "$candidate" -c 'import sys; raise SystemExit(0 if sys.version_info >= (3, 11) else 1)' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    PYTHON_BIN=$(command -v "$candidate")
    break
  fi
done

if [[ -z "$PYTHON_BIN" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: Python 3.11 or newer is required." >&2
  echo "Install Python 3.11+ or rerun with PYTHON_BIN=/path/to/python3.11 ./scripts/install.sh" >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "Using Python: $PYTHON_BIN ($($PYTHON_BIN --version 2>&1))"
APP_VERSION=$(sed -n 's/^__version__[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)"/\1/p' "$SELF_DIR/app/version.py" | head -1)
[[ -n "$APP_VERSION" ]] || { echo "ERROR: unable to read app version" >&2; exit 1; }
echo "OpenCode Multiuser version: $APP_VERSION"

USER_UID=$(id -u)
export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/run/user/${USER_UID}}
export DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=${DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS:-unix:path=${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/bus}

if [[ ! -d "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR" || ! -S "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bus" ]]; then
  cat >&2 <<EOF
ERROR: the systemd user runtime/bus is not available for $USER (UID $USER_UID).
Expected:
  $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR
  $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bus

Run as root (or via sudo):
  loginctl enable-linger $USER
  systemctl start user-runtime-dir@${USER_UID}.service
  systemctl start user@${USER_UID}.service

Then log in again as $USER and rerun the installer.
Do not manually create /run/user/${USER_UID}.
EOF
  exit 1
fi

if ! systemctl --user show-environment >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "ERROR: systemctl --user cannot reach the user manager via $DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS" >&2
  exit 1
fi

CGROUP_CTRL="/sys/fs/cgroup/user.slice/user-${USER_UID}.slice/user@${USER_UID}.service/cgroup.controllers"
if [[ -r "$CGROUP_CTRL" ]]; then
  controllers=" $(cat "$CGROUP_CTRL") "
  missing=()
  for ctrl in cpu memory pids; do
    [[ "$controllers" == *" $ctrl "* ]] || missing+=("$ctrl")
  done
  if (( ${#missing[@]} )); then
    cat >&2 <<EOF
ERROR: missing delegated cgroup controllers for rootless Podman: ${missing[*]}
Current controllers: $(cat "$CGROUP_CTRL")

Configure the host as root, for example:
  mkdir -p /etc/systemd/system/user@.service.d
  cat > /etc/systemd/system/user@.service.d/delegate.conf <<'EOC'
[Service]
Delegate=cpu cpuset io memory pids
EOC
  systemctl daemon-reload
  systemctl restart user@${USER_UID}.service

Then log in again as $USER and rerun the installer.
EOF
    exit 1
  fi
else
  echo "WARNING: could not read $CGROUP_CTRL; CPU/memory/pids delegation could not be preflighted." >&2
fi

TARGET="$HOME/opt/opencode-multiuser"
CFG="$HOME/.config/opencode-multiuser"
QUADLET="$HOME/.config/containers/systemd"
USER_SYSTEMD="$HOME/.config/systemd/user"

mkdir -p "$TARGET" "$CFG" "$QUADLET" "$USER_SYSTEMD"

# On upgrades, reuse persisted public host and port unless explicitly overridden.
if [[ -f "$CFG/control-plane.env" ]]; then
  if [[ -z "${BASE_DOMAIN_EXPLICIT:-}" ]]; then
    persisted_domain=$(sed -n 's/^BASE_DOMAIN=//p' "$CFG/control-plane.env" | tail -1)
    [[ -n "$persisted_domain" ]] && BASE_DOMAIN=$persisted_domain
  fi
  if [[ -z "${CONTROL_PLANE_PORT_EXPLICIT:-}" ]]; then
    persisted_port=$(sed -n 's/^CONTROL_PLANE_PORT=//p' "$CFG/control-plane.env" | tail -1)
    [[ -n "$persisted_port" ]] && CONTROL_PLANE_PORT=$persisted_port
  fi
  if [[ -z "${OPENCODE_VERSION_EXPLICIT:-}" ]]; then
    persisted_opencode_version=$(sed -n 's/^OPENCODE_VERSION=//p' "$CFG/control-plane.env" | tail -1)
    [[ -n "$persisted_opencode_version" ]] && OPENCODE_VERSION=$persisted_opencode_version
  fi
  if [[ -z "${OPENCODE_ENABLED_PROVIDERS_EXPLICIT:-}" ]]; then
    persisted_enabled_providers=$(sed -n 's/^OPENCODE_ENABLED_PROVIDERS=//p' "$CFG/control-plane.env" | tail -1)
    OPENCODE_ENABLED_PROVIDERS=$persisted_enabled_providers
  fi
  if [[ -z "${OPENCODE_DISABLED_PROVIDERS_EXPLICIT:-}" ]]; then
    persisted_disabled_providers=$(sed -n 's/^OPENCODE_DISABLED_PROVIDERS=//p' "$CFG/control-plane.env" | tail -1)
    OPENCODE_DISABLED_PROVIDERS=$persisted_disabled_providers
  fi
  if [[ -z "${DATA_ROOT_EXPLICIT:-}" ]]; then
    persisted_data_root=$(sed -n 's/^DATA_ROOT=//p' "$CFG/control-plane.env" | tail -1)
    [[ -n "$persisted_data_root" ]] && DATA_ROOT=$persisted_data_root
  fi
  if [[ -z "${TRAEFIK_DYNAMIC_DIR_EXPLICIT:-}" ]]; then
    persisted_traefik_dynamic_dir=$(sed -n 's/^TRAEFIK_DYNAMIC_DIR=//p' "$CFG/control-plane.env" | tail -1)
    [[ -n "$persisted_traefik_dynamic_dir" ]] && TRAEFIK_DYNAMIC_DIR=$persisted_traefik_dynamic_dir
  fi
fi

DATA_ROOT=${DATA_ROOT//%h/$HOME}
TRAEFIK_DYNAMIC_DIR=${TRAEFIK_DYNAMIC_DIR//%h/$HOME}
DATA_ROOT=${DATA_ROOT:-"$HOME/.local/share/opencode-multiuser"}
TRAEFIK_DYNAMIC_DIR=${TRAEFIK_DYNAMIC_DIR:-"$DATA_ROOT/traefik-dynamic"}
if [[ "$DATA_ROOT" != /* || "$TRAEFIK_DYNAMIC_DIR" != /* ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: DATA_ROOT and TRAEFIK_DYNAMIC_DIR must be absolute paths." >&2
  exit 1
fi
TRAEFIK_STATE_DIR="$DATA_ROOT/traefik"
mkdir -p "$DATA_ROOT" "$TRAEFIK_DYNAMIC_DIR" "$TRAEFIK_STATE_DIR"

systemctl --user stop opencode-control-plane.service >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

if command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1 && ss -H -ltn "sport = :${CONTROL_PLANE_PORT}" 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
  cat >&2 <<EOF
ERROR: CONTROL_PLANE_PORT=${CONTROL_PLANE_PORT} is already in use.
Choose another free port, for example:
  CONTROL_PLANE_PORT=8011 PYTHON_BIN=${PYTHON_BIN} ./scripts/install.sh
EOF
  exit 1
fi

rsync -a --delete --exclude .venv --exclude .pytest_cache "$SELF_DIR/" "$TARGET/"

for required_file in app/portal.py app/ui.py app/oidc.py app/opencode_update.py app/version.py uv.lock; do
  if [[ ! -f "$TARGET/$required_file" ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: upgrade copy is incomplete: $TARGET/$required_file was not installed." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done
cp "$TARGET/systemd/quadlet/"* "$QUADLET/"
DATA_ROOT_SED=$(printf '%s' "$DATA_ROOT" | sed 's/[&|\\]/\\&/g')
TRAEFIK_DYNAMIC_DIR_SED=$(printf '%s' "$TRAEFIK_DYNAMIC_DIR" | sed 's/[&|\\]/\\&/g')
TRAEFIK_STATE_DIR_SED=$(printf '%s' "$TRAEFIK_STATE_DIR" | sed 's/[&|\\]/\\&/g')
sed \
  -e "s|__TRAEFIK_DYNAMIC_DIR__|$TRAEFIK_DYNAMIC_DIR_SED|g" \
  -e "s|__TRAEFIK_STATE_DIR__|$TRAEFIK_STATE_DIR_SED|g" \
  "$TARGET/systemd/quadlet/traefik.container" > "$QUADLET/traefik.container"
cp "$TARGET/systemd/opencode-control-plane.service" "$USER_SYSTEMD/"
cp "$TARGET/traefik/traefik.yml" "$CFG/traefik.yml"

if [[ ! -f "$CFG/postgres.env" ]]; then
  POSTGRES_PASSWORD=$(openssl rand -hex 24)
  printf 'POSTGRES_PASSWORD=%s\n' "$POSTGRES_PASSWORD" > "$CFG/postgres.env"
  chmod 600 "$CFG/postgres.env"
else
  POSTGRES_PASSWORD=$(sed -n 's/^POSTGRES_PASSWORD=//p' "$CFG/postgres.env")
fi

if [[ ! -f "$CFG/control-plane.env" ]]; then
  JWT_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
  cat > "$CFG/control-plane.env" <<ENV
BASE_DOMAIN=$BASE_DOMAIN
CONTROL_PLANE_BIND=$CONTROL_PLANE_BIND
CONTROL_PLANE_PORT=$CONTROL_PLANE_PORT
CONTROL_PLANE_URL=http://$BASE_DOMAIN:$TRAEFIK_PUBLIC_PORT
TRAEFIK_ENTRYPOINT=$TRAEFIK_ENTRYPOINT
DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://opencode:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@127.0.0.1:5432/opencode
JWT_SECRET=$JWT_SECRET
LOCAL_AUTH_ENABLED=true
ALLOW_REGISTRATION=true
OIDC_ENABLED=false
OIDC_ISSUER=
OIDC_DISCOVERY_URL=
OIDC_CLIENT_ID=
OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=

OIDC_DISPLAY_NAME=Corporate SSO
OIDC_REDIRECT_URI=
OIDC_USE_PKCE=true

OIDC_DEFAULT_ROLE=developer

OIDC_EMAIL_CLAIM=email
OIDC_NAME_CLAIM=name
OIDC_STATE_COOKIE_NAME=oc_oidc_state
OIDC_STATE_TTL_SECONDS=600

WORKSPACE_COOKIE_NAME=oc_workspace
COOKIE_SECURE=false

WORKSPACE_IMAGE=localhost/opencode-workspace:latest

OPENCODE_REGISTRY_URL=https://registry.npmjs.org/opencode-ai/latest
OPENCODE_UPDATE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=900
PODMAN_NETWORK=opencode-net
DATA_ROOT=$DATA_ROOT
MAX_SLOTS=10
WORKSPACE_MEMORY=8g
WORKSPACE_CPUS=4
WORKSPACE_PIDS_LIMIT=1024

WORKSPACE_READY_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS=0.5

WORKSPACE_REAPER_INTERVAL_SECONDS=60

WORKSPACE_HOST_PORT_BASE=$WORKSPACE_HOST_PORT_BASE
OPENCODE_ENABLED_PROVIDERS=$OPENCODE_ENABLED_PROVIDERS
OPENCODE_DISABLED_PROVIDERS=$OPENCODE_DISABLED_PROVIDERS
TRAEFIK_DYNAMIC_DIR=$TRAEFIK_DYNAMIC_DIR
TRAEFIK_TLS=false
TRAEFIK_CERT_RESOLVER=letsencrypt
ENV
  chmod 600 "$CFG/control-plane.env"
else

  grep -q '^CONTROL_PLANE_BIND=' "$CFG/control-plane.env" || echo "CONTROL_PLANE_BIND=$CONTROL_PLANE_BIND" >> "$CFG/control-plane.env"

  grep -q '^TRAEFIK_ENTRYPOINT=' "$CFG/control-plane.env" || echo "TRAEFIK_ENTRYPOINT=$TRAEFIK_ENTRYPOINT" >> "$CFG/control-plane.env"
  grep -q '^SESSION_COOKIE_NAME=' "$CFG/control-plane.env" || echo "SESSION_COOKIE_NAME=oc_session" >> "$CFG/control-plane.env"
  grep -q '^WORKSPACE_COOKIE_NAME=' "$CFG/control-plane.env" || echo "WORKSPACE_COOKIE_NAME=oc_workspace" >> "$CFG/control-plane.env"

  grep -q '^OIDC_DISCOVERY_URL=' "$CFG/control-plane.env" || echo "OIDC_DISCOVERY_URL=" >> "$CFG/control-plane.env"

  grep -q '^OIDC_SCOPES=' "$CFG/control-plane.env" || echo "OIDC_SCOPES=openid profile email" >> "$CFG/control-plane.env"
  grep -q '^OIDC_DISPLAY_NAME=' "$CFG/control-plane.env" || echo "OIDC_DISPLAY_NAME=Corporate SSO" >> "$CFG/control-plane.env"

  grep -q '^OIDC_USERNAME_CLAIM=' "$CFG/control-plane.env" || echo "OIDC_USERNAME_CLAIM=preferred_username" >> "$CFG/control-plane.env"

  if [[ -n "${DATA_ROOT_EXPLICIT:-}" ]]; then

  # Older releases may have persisted an HTTPS public URL even while Traefik
  # was deliberately running without TLS. Normalize that known upgrade case so
  # browser cookies and /open/<workspace> redirects remain on working HTTP.
  EFFECTIVE_TRAEFIK_TLS=$(sed -n 's/^TRAEFIK_TLS=//p' "$CFG/control-plane.env" | tail -1 | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
  CURRENT_PUBLIC_URL=$(sed -n 's/^CONTROL_PLANE_URL=//p' "$CFG/control-plane.env" | tail -1)
  if [[ "${EFFECTIVE_TRAEFIK_TLS:-false}" != "true" && "$CURRENT_PUBLIC_URL" == https://$BASE_DOMAIN* ]]; then
    sed -i "s|^CONTROL_PLANE_URL=.*|CONTROL_PLANE_URL=http://$BASE_DOMAIN:$TRAEFIK_PUBLIC_PORT|" "$CFG/control-plane.env"
  fi
fi

# An explicit installer override becomes the new persisted engine version.
if [[ -n "${OPENCODE_VERSION_EXPLICIT:-}" ]]; then
  if grep -q '^OPENCODE_VERSION=' "$CFG/control-plane.env"; then
    sed -i "s/^OPENCODE_VERSION=.*/OPENCODE_VERSION=$OPENCODE_VERSION/" "$CFG/control-plane.env"
  else
    echo "OPENCODE_VERSION=$OPENCODE_VERSION" >> "$CFG/control-plane.env"
  fi
fi

# Provider policy overrides are persisted just like an explicit OpenCode
# version. Provider IDs are comma-separated, so escape only sed metacharacters.
for provider_policy_key in OPENCODE_ENABLED_PROVIDERS OPENCODE_DISABLED_PROVIDERS; do
  explicit_name="${provider_policy_key}_EXPLICIT"
  if [[ -n "${!explicit_name:-}" ]]; then
    provider_policy_value=${!provider_policy_key}
    provider_policy_sed=$(printf '%s' "$provider_policy_value" | sed 's/[&|\\]/\\&/g')

      sed -i "s|^${provider_policy_key}=.*|${provider_policy_key}=${provider_policy_sed}|" "$CFG/control-plane.env"

sed \
  -e "s|__BASE_DOMAIN__|$BASE_DOMAIN|g" \
  -e "s|__CONTROL_PLANE_PORT__|$EFFECTIVE_CONTROL_PLANE_PORT|g" \
  -e "s|__TRAEFIK_ENTRYPOINT__|$EFFECTIVE_TRAEFIK_ENTRYPOINT|g" \

# Remove v5 per-workspace hostname routes. v6 proxies every workspace through

sleep 2

Public gateway:

scripts/package-release.sh.summary: Builds a release archive `opencode-multiuser-<version>.zip` plus a `.sha256` checksum file from the repository tree. The version is read from `scripts/version.py show`, and the archive is staged with `rsync` (excluding `.git`, virtualenvs, caches and build output) before being zipped.

notes.text: Resolves the repository root from the script location, so it works from any current directory. `PYTHON_BIN` can be overridden, and the first argument sets the output directory (default `<root>/dist`). The version is obtained by running `version.py show`, which keeps one source of truth for the number.
Stages the copy in a temporary directory that the `EXIT` trap deletes, even if a later step fails.
Checks that `rsync` and `zip` exist before doing any work and exits with a clear error if not.

Copies the tree into `<stage>/<name>/` with `rsync -a`, leaving out VCS data, virtualenvs, caches, build output and the `dist` directory. Excluding `dist` stops earlier archives from being packed into new ones. The top-level folder is named `<name>` so the zip unpacks into a single versioned directory.
Removes any previous zip and checksum for this version so a rebuild never leaves stale files.
Zips from inside the staging directory so archive paths start at `<name>/` and do not include the temporary path. `-q` quiets the output and `-r` recurses.

Runs `sha256sum` from inside `DIST_DIR`, so the checksum file holds a bare filename and `sha256sum -c` works when the zip and checksum sit together. `sha256sum` is the GNU tool name, which is not present on every platform.
Prints the two output paths, one per line, so callers can read them from stdout.

scripts/package-release.sh.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
PYTHON_BIN=${PYTHON_BIN:-python3}
VERSION=$($PYTHON_BIN "$ROOT/scripts/version.py" show)
NAME="opencode-multiuser-${VERSION}"
DIST_DIR=${1:-"$ROOT/dist"}
STAGE=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$STAGE"' EXIT

command -v rsync >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "ERROR: rsync is required" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v zip >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "ERROR: zip is required" >&2; exit 1; }

mkdir -p "$DIST_DIR" "$STAGE/$NAME"
rsync -a \
  --exclude '.git' \
  --exclude '.venv' \
  --exclude '.pytest_cache' \
  --exclude '__pycache__' \
  --exclude '*.pyc' \
  --exclude 'build' \
  --exclude '*.egg-info' \
  --exclude 'dist' \
  "$ROOT/" "$STAGE/$NAME/"

rm -f "$DIST_DIR/$NAME.zip" "$DIST_DIR/$NAME.zip.sha256"
(
  cd "$STAGE"
  zip -qr "$DIST_DIR/$NAME.zip" "$NAME"
)
(
  cd "$DIST_DIR"
  sha256sum "$NAME.zip" > "$NAME.zip.sha256"
)

echo "$DIST_DIR/$NAME.zip"
echo "$DIST_DIR/$NAME.zip.sha256"

scripts/reset-orphans.sh.summary: Cleanup helper that force-removes leftover OpenCode workspace containers from Podman. The name filter is strict on purpose, so only dynamically allocated workspace containers are touched and fixed services such as PostgreSQL and Traefik are not.

notes.text: States the safety contract: only dynamically allocated workspace containers are removed.

Lists all containers, running or stopped, by name. `awk` keeps only names matching `^oc-<digits>-<hex>$`, which is the shape the comment calls dynamically allocated. The kept names are passed to `podman rm -f`, which stops and removes them. `xargs -r` skips `podman rm` when nothing matched, so the script is a no-op on a clean host. Container names that do not fit the pattern are never selected.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
# Removes only dynamically allocated OpenCode workspace containers.
podman ps -a --format '{{.Names}}' | awk '/^oc-[0-9]+-[a-f0-9]+$/' | xargs -r podman rm -f

scripts/version.py.summary: Small CLI that shows, sets or bumps the project's Semantic Version. The only stored copy of the version is the `__version__ = "X.Y.Z"` line in `app/version.py`. This script edits it in place and accepts only strict `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. `package-release.sh` calls its `show` command to name the release archive.

notes.text: `ROOT` is found relative to this file, so the script works from any working directory. `SEMVER_RE` allows no leading zeros. `ASSIGNMENT_RE` uses `re.MULTILINE` so `^` and `$` match at line boundaries and only a top-level `__version__ = "..."` line is matched.
`count=1` limits the substitution to the first match, and `subn` also returns the number of replacements for the check on line 45.
Validates first, then splits on dots and converts each part to an int in one generator expression.
Any `part` other than major or minor takes the patch branch, relying on the argparse `choices` in `main` to prevent bad values.
`args.command or "show"` makes running the script with no arguments print the current version.

scripts/version.py.text:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Show, set, or bump the OpenCode Multiuser Semantic Version.

Examples:
    python3 scripts/version.py show
    python3 scripts/version.py bump patch
    python3 scripts/version.py bump minor
    python3 scripts/version.py bump major
    python3 scripts/version.py set 0.11.2
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import re
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
VERSION_FILE = ROOT / "app" / "version.py"
SEMVER_RE = re.compile(r"^(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*)$")
ASSIGNMENT_RE = re.compile(r'^__version__\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"\s*$', re.MULTILINE)


def read_version() -> str:
    text = VERSION_FILE.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    match = ASSIGNMENT_RE.search(text)
    if not match:
        raise SystemExit(f"Could not find __version__ in {VERSION_FILE}")
    version = match.group(1)
    if not SEMVER_RE.fullmatch(version):
        raise SystemExit(f"Invalid Semantic Version in {VERSION_FILE}: {version}")
    return version


def validate(version: str) -> str:
    if not SEMVER_RE.fullmatch(version):
        raise SystemExit("Version must use MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, for example 0.11.1")
    return version


def write_version(version: str) -> None:
    version = validate(version)
    text = VERSION_FILE.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    updated, count = ASSIGNMENT_RE.subn(f'__version__ = "{version}"', text, count=1)
    if count != 1:
        raise SystemExit(f"Could not update __version__ in {VERSION_FILE}")
    VERSION_FILE.write_text(updated, encoding="utf-8")


def bump(version: str, part: str) -> str:
    major, minor, patch = (int(x) for x in validate(version).split("."))
    if part == "major":
        return f"{major + 1}.0.0"
    if part == "minor":
        return f"{major}.{minor + 1}.0"
    return f"{major}.{minor}.{patch + 1}"


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Manage the OpenCode Multiuser Semantic Version")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command")
    sub.add_parser("show", help="Print the current version")
    set_parser = sub.add_parser("set", help="Set an explicit MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH version")
    set_parser.add_argument("version")
    bump_parser = sub.add_parser("bump", help="Increment part of the Semantic Version")
    bump_parser.add_argument("part", choices=("major", "minor", "patch"))
    args = parser.parse_args()

    command = args.command or "show"
    current = read_version()
    if command == "show":
        print(current)
        return
    if command == "set":
        new = validate(args.version)
    else:
        new = bump(current, args.part)
    write_version(new)
    print(f"{current} -> {new}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

tests/test_gateway.py.summary: The main test module of the repository. Despite its name it covers much more than the gateway: Traefik URL and route cleanup, runtime helpers (host ports, per-workspace data directories, managed OpenCode provider policy, readiness polling), workspace deletion, the portal widget and HTML pages, role and OIDC provisioning, admin protections and OpenCode version validation. Most tests use `monkeypatch` to redirect `settings` values such as `data_root` to a pytest `tmp_path`, and in-memory SQLite for database-backed cases.

notes.text: Overrides the setting on the module object used by `traefik`, so the URL builder sees the test value; `monkeypatch` restores it afterwards.
Provider list is deliberately messy (extra space, duplicate `anthropic`) to test parsing and de-duplication.
Pins the policy file location, its exact JSON content and its permissions (`0o644`).
Fake Podman runner: records the argument list and returns an object with the attributes the real result exposes.
Replaces process-spawning and readiness-waiting helpers so `start_workspace` runs without Podman or a network.
Selects the `podman run -d` invocation among all recorded commands; `next` raises `StopIteration` if none was issued.
The mount source is the policy file under the data root and the target is OpenCode's system-wide config path, with `ro` for read-only and `Z` for SELinux labelling.
Fixes the cookie names so the test can use fixed names in the cookie header.
The client's bearer token is replaced by the server-injected Basic credential; routing headers and `Host` are removed; the portal's own cookies are stripped but other cookies pass through.
Sets up a legacy per-workspace route file next to the control-plane route file, which must be preserved.
Both `.` and `..` must raise `ValueError`; the `assert False` in the `try` fails the test if no exception occurs.
Imports inside the test keep SQLAlchemy and the FastAPI app out of module import time.
Creates a throwaway in-memory SQLite database with the full schema.
Creates the on-disk workspace directories so the test can later show they were deleted.
Calls the endpoint function directly, bypassing HTTP, with the owner as the acting user.
Checks that both the database row and the data directory were removed.
Patches the container check and the HTTP connection class used by `runtime`, then calls the readiness wait with a container name, a port and a secret.
Ensures the widget is injected before the closing `</body>`, using a case-insensitive search for the last closing tag.
Idempotency check: the marker element must appear exactly once after two injections.
The header lookup is lower-case, so the forwarded header map uses lower-case keys for this header.
The partial index must cover active states (`RUNNING`) and exclude `STOPPED`, so stopped rows do not block creating a new workspace for the same project.
Pins the CSS grid layout of the start field so the help text sits under the input, not beside the button.
First user becomes `admin`; after one user exists the next gets `developer`.
Calls provisioning twice with the same claims to check it is stable and does not create duplicate users.
Expected `admin` despite `oidc_default_role` being `developer`: the first-user bootstrap rule takes precedence.
The guard raises 409 while `root` is the only enabled admin; once a second enabled admin exists the same call passes.

card.summary: Background coroutine that periodically reconciles stale runtimes and reaps idle workspaces.
card.details: It sleeps for `max(5, settings.workspace_reaper_interval_seconds)` seconds, then runs `_reconcile_workspace_runtimes` and `_reap_idle_workspaces` in worker threads with `asyncio.to_thread` so the event loop is not blocked. Any exception is logged and the loop continues.
card.notes: `asyncio.CancelledError` is re-raised explicitly so that cancelling the task during shutdown works, while other errors do not kill the loop. The interval has a floor of 5 seconds.

card.summary: FastAPI lifespan context manager that prepares the database, slots, directories and routes at startup and stops the reaper at shutdown.
card.details: On startup it validates auth settings, drops the legacy workspace constraint, migrates the user auth schema, creates tables, seeds slots, creates the data and Traefik dynamic directories, and removes legacy per-workspace Traefik route files. It then reconciles stale runtimes, dedupes active workspaces, and creates the active-workspace index. If the idle timeout is positive it starts `_idle_reaper_loop` as a task. On shutdown the task is cancelled and awaited.
card.notes: The order matters. The legacy constraint is dropped before `create_all`, and dedupe runs before the index creation. `asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True)` stops the cancellation from raising at shutdown.

params.app: The `FastAPI` instance; not used in the body.

card.summary: Starts, or reuses, the workspace for a project and allocates a runtime slot for it.

If it is `STARTING` or `RUNNING` and is healthy enough (running, secret file present, container running), it just touches the activity timestamp and returns it. Otherwise it is released with reason `recycle`. A free slot is then selected (on non-SQLite with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`) and the slot is reserved and committed. After that `start_workspace` creates the container, and the workspace is marked `RUNNING`.
card.notes: A 503 is returned when no slot is free. If `start_workspace` fails, the container is stopped, the slot freed, and the workspace set to `ERROR` before a 500 is raised. An existing row is reused (new slot, `STARTING`, reset `created_at`) instead of inserting a new one. The reuse check differs from `_workspace_runtime_usable` because it does not check the slot port.

Browser navigations are then redirected to `/dashboard?reason=backend&workspace=...` with the workspace cookie deleted. Other clients get a 409 with the code `workspace_backend_unavailable`. A usable workspace is proxied through `proxy_http`. If an `HTTPException` with status 404 or 409 comes out of the block, `_idle_timeout_response` is tried first, so a workspace reclaimed for inactivity gets the idle response instead of a generic error. Any other exception is re-raised.

This route must stay registered after all the control-plane routes, as the comment above it says. The function has no decorator on the lines shown here; its `@app.api_route` decorator is on line 948.

Authentication and workspace selection happen inside `proxy_websocket`, which is not shown in this part. card.summary: Upgrades a pre-existing `users` table (v6.5 and older) with role, auth provider and OIDC identity columns, then backfills sensible values.
card.details: Returns immediately if `users` does not exist, since a fresh database is created from the current model. PostgreSQL uses `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` and drops `NOT NULL` on `password_hash` so OIDC-only accounts can have no password. SQLite inspects the existing columns and adds only the missing ones. After that, empty roles become `developer`, empty providers become `local`, and the oldest user is promoted to `admin` if no admin exists.
card.notes: Everything runs in one `engine.begin()` transaction. On SQLite the legacy `NOT NULL` on `password_hash` is kept, as the docstring says. Unsupported dialects log a warning and return early, before any backfill. The `NOT NULL`/`DEFAULT` constraints on `role` and `auth_provider` are applied only on PostgreSQL, and only after the backfill, so existing rows cannot violate them. The unique partial index on `(oidc_issuer, oidc_subject)` is created with `IF NOT EXISTS`, so the function is safe to run on every start.

card.summary: Removes the old `uq_activeish_workspace` constraint from `workspaces` so it no longer conflicts with the newer partial index.
card.details: On PostgreSQL it runs `ALTER TABLE IF EXISTS ... DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS`, so it is a no-op when the table or constraint is absent. On SQLite it only logs and does nothing.
card.notes: SQLite cannot drop a constraint in place, so a legacy SQLite database keeps the constraint. Other dialects are silently ignored.

card.summary: Creates the partial unique index `uq_active_workspace` on `workspaces (user_id, project_slug)`, limited to rows whose status is STARTING, RUNNING or STOPPING.
card.details: This enforces at the database level that a user can have at most one non-stopped workspace per project, while any number of STOPPED or ERROR rows may coexist. It is created with `IF NOT EXISTS`, so repeated calls are harmless.
card.notes: The status literals are the uppercase enum member names. Dialects other than PostgreSQL and SQLite log a warning and get no index, so the invariant is then not enforced by the database.

card.summary: Returns the current time as a timezone-aware UTC `datetime`.
card.notes: Used as the callable default for `created_at` columns, so it is evaluated per insert, not once at import.

card.summary: Lifecycle states of a workspace: starting, running, stopping, stopped, error.
card.details: It subclasses `str` and `enum.Enum`, so members compare equal to their string values and serialize naturally.
card.notes: The `Workspace.status` column stores this through SQLAlchemy `Enum(WorkspaceStatus)`. The partial index predicate lists `'STARTING','RUNNING','STOPPING'` in uppercase, which are the member names, not the lowercase values.

card.summary: The two roles a user can have: `admin` and `developer`.

card.summary: Account table for both local-password and OIDC users.

card.notes: The `uq_oidc_identity` partial unique index on `(oidc_issuer, oidc_subject)` applies only when `oidc_subject IS NOT NULL`, so any number of local users with NULL OIDC columns are allowed. `app/migrations.py` creates the same index for older databases. `username` is unique and indexed.

card.summary: One entry in the fixed pool of concurrent-workspace slots. `in_use` marks it as taken and `workspace_id` records the owner.

card.summary: A user's workspace for one project, together with the slot it occupies, its container name and its status.

card.notes: The `uq_active_workspace` partial unique index on `(user_id, project_slug)` for statuses STARTING, RUNNING and STOPPING means a second concurrent start of the same project fails with an integrity error at the database level. Stopped and error rows are not constrained.

card.summary: Registers the `generic_oidc` client with the Authlib `OAuth` registry once, using the configured client id, secret, discovery URL and scopes.

The streamed output is collected and returned in a `CompletedProcess`.

card.summary: Background worker that builds, tests and activates a new OpenCode image, recording progress and any failure in `_STATE`.

It then runs the candidate with `--version` and requires the reported version to equal the requested one. Only then does it tag the candidate as `settings.workspace_image` and call `_persist_version`.
card.notes: The live image is retagged only after the smoke test passes, so a failed build or test leaves the current image untouched, and the candidate tag is kept for diagnosis. Running workspaces are not changed. Only newly started ones use the new image. Any exception is caught and recorded as status `error`, and `finally` sets `previous_version` if it is still unset. A `+` in the version is replaced by `_` for the image tag.

card.summary: Chooses the role for a newly created account: `admin` if no users exist yet, otherwise the requested default role.
